title: Firm Productivity and the Composition of Jobs in the Green Economy: Factor Reallocation with Heterogeneous Clean Destinations
content: We study the macroeconomic consequences of emissions reductions in a model with heterogeneous firms, search-and-matching frictions, endogenous technology adoption, and sector-specific capital adjustment costs. Extending the framework of Finkelstein Shapiro and Metcalf (2023) and calibrating to Finland, we distinguish between high- and low-productivity clean technologies within a three-sector framework. Our results show that an emission reduction policy implemented via a carbon tax induces modest losses in output and consumption, as part of the reallocation away from emissions-intensive sector is absorbed by lower-productivity clean sector. By contrast, the standard two-sector model with a single clean technology shows slightly positive output effects due to a greater increase in average firm productivity. These findings highlight that the macroeconomic costs of climate policies depend on the productivity composition of the expanding clean sector. Within the emissions-intensive sector, emissions are mainly reduced through abatement activities, but the degree of factor reallocation is still substantial: under the baseline calibration, employment in the emissions-intensive sector declines by nearly one-quarter in response to a 40% emissions reduction target. Lower abatement costs reduce the extent of factor reallocation required to achieve a given emissions reduction target.

title: RSV on ikääntyneille merkittävä terveysriski – voi altistaa sydän- ja verisuonikomplikaatioille
content:
Marraskuun alussa vietetään kansainvälistä RSV-tietoisuusviikkoa. Suomessa RSV-kausi käynnistyy yleensä marras–joulukuussa, ja tartuntoja on eniten vuodenvaihteen molemmin puolin. Virukselle on tyypillistä syklinen esiintyminen, jolloin voimakkaampi RSV-epidemia toistuu noin joka toinen vuosi.

Suomessa laboratoriovarmistettuja RSV-tapauksia todetaan vuosittain noin 4000–8000, epidemiakauden voimakkuudesta riippuen. Todellinen tartuntojen määrä on kuitenkin virallisia tilastoja suurempi, sillä valtaosa lieväoireisista hengitystieinfektioista sairastetaan kotona ilman laboratoriotestejä.

RSV voi aiheuttaa ikääntyneille vaikean taudin ja olla pahimmillaan hengenvaarallinen

RSV on merkittävä vakavan infektion aiheuttaja pienten lasten lisäksi myös ikääntyneillä. Ikäihmisillä RSV voi johtaa sairaalahoitoon ja siihen voi liittyä huomattava kuolleisuusriski. Riski sairastua vaikeaan tautimuotoon kasvaa iän myötä, etenkin jos henkilöllä on perussairauksia.

title: HIKET at Climate Currents: Looking ahead to COP31
content:
HIKET project took part in the Climate Currents event “What to expect for COP31?”, organized by University of Helsinki and Aalto University at Tiedekulma on 27 October. The event brought together researchers, policymakers, business representatives and young people to explore the key issues ahead of COP31 and the wider COP process.

HIKET’s objectives for COP31, presented by Research Director Tuomo Kalliokoski, include developing wider research cooperation to support land-sector climate decisions at the global level.  

Another key objective is connecting research with climate action. HIKET research bridges the gap between science, policy and business, which supports implementation of the Paris Agreement.  

Reliable evidence for effective AFOLU mitigation actions ensures engagement of policymakers and creates new opportunities for business applications.

The desired outcome: shared interest, identified partners and agreed next steps.

title: Pohjoismaisen kirjallisuusviikon vieras Michaela von Kügelgen Lahden pääkirjastossa 9.11.
content:
Pohjoismaisen kirjallisuusviikon vieraana nähdään kirjailija, toimittaja ja yrittäjä, joka kuvaa teoksissaan pohjoismaista arkea, perhettä ja työn ja elämän yhteensovittamista.


Pohjoismaisen kirjallisuusviikon 9.–15.11. merkeissä Lahden pääkirjastoon saapuu vieraaksi suomenruotsalainen kirjailija Michaela von Kügelgen.

Von Kügelgenilta on ilmestynyt kansainvälisen läpimurron tehnyt hyvän mielen Villa Hilda -sarja, jonka käännösoikeudet myytiin seitsemään maahan, ja elokuva- ja tv-oikeudet varmistuivat heti julkaisun jälkeen. Hän kirjoittaa yhdessä Anne Hietasen kanssa Koski & Fors -dekkarisarjaa, jonka ensimmäinen osa Viimeinen piste julkaistiin elokuussa 2026. Von Kügelgen myös pitää kirjoittamaan innostavaa Kugge skriver -blogia.

Pohjoismaisen kirjallisuusviikon käynnistävä kirjailijailta pidetään Lahden pääkirjaston tapahtuma-alueella maanantaina 9.11. klo 18–19. Haastattelijana toimii kirjastonhoitaja Angelika Nikkinen. Keskustelu käydään suomeksi.

Kaikille avoin ja maksuton tilaisuus järjestetään yhteistyössä Lahden Pohjola-Nordenin kanssa.

title: Fem projekt fick stöd från de ungas kultur- och språkprogram Volt
content:
De samlade projektansökningarna representerar såväl uttrycksformer som film, litteratur och fotografi som ljudkonst och poesi. Projekten har närmat sig tillhörighet på många sätt.

– De projekt som fått höga poäng har haft väldigt konkreta ansökningar och en taktil approach till hur man går till väga för att förstå tillhörighet, säger Randi Samsonsen, den beslutsfattande sakkunniggruppens ordförande.

– Ett gemensamt kriterium för de som stöds är också att de barn och unga som projektet berör verkligen möts i det verkliga livet, att saker ska ha möjlighet att uppstå genom verkliga möten. Bland de stödda projekten är detta ett kvalitetsperspektiv, och inte bara ett kvantitetsperspektiv, förklarar Samsonsen. 

Nordic Lunch Stories är ett ungdomsdrivet grönt konstprojekt som för samman 12–15-åringar från Finland, Sverige och Danmark. Genom ljud, berättande, scenkonst och matkultur skapar ungdomarna tillsammans ett konstnärsresidens, ett flerspråkigt ljudlandskap och en offentlig presentation om hur vi kan leva hållbart i vardagen.

title: Suden matkassa -näyttely huipentuu taiteilijatapaamiseen
content:
Lokakuun ajan Ikimetsägalleriassa esillä ollut Suden matkassa -näyttely huipentuu lauantaina 7.11. taiteilijatapaamiseen, jossa taide, metsät ja musiikki kohtaavat.

Näyttelyn teokset tarkastelevat sutta luonnon monimuotoisuuden, rinnakkaiselon ja ihmisen luontosuhteen näkökulmista. Mukana ovat kuvataiteilijat Samuli Heimonen ja Minna Pyykkö sekä valokuvataiteilija Juha Suonpää, joiden lähestymistavat samaan aiheeseen ovat keskenään hyvin erilaisia.

Päivän ohjelma käynnistyy klo 12.30 Juha Suonpään esityksellä Kun metsä vielä katsoo. Videoista koostuva esitys rakentuu seitsemän vuoden aikana metsään sijoitettujen kameroiden tallentamista hetkistä sekä tekstistä, äänestä ja hiljaisuudesta. Teos tarkastelee metsän läsnäoloa, muistia ja katoamista sekä elämää, joka jatkuu omassa rytmissään ihmisen katseen ulottumattomissa.

Esityksen jälkeen Suonpää, Pyykkö ja Heimonen kertovat taiteestaan, työskentelystään ja näyttelyn taustoista. Tilaisuus tarjoaa harvinaisen mahdollisuuden keskustella taiteilijoiden kanssa heidän teoksistaan ja susiaiheen herättämistä ajatuksista.

title: A Beginner’s Guide to Philosophy: From Logic to Epistemology to Metaphysics
content:
These are, perhaps, not the very best times for humanities majors. Seldom do we even hear the once-standard defense that, by pursuing a course of study in subjects of that kind, students “learn how to think.” Such a justification still points to real value, at least in the most demanding settings. Take Harvard’s course Humanities 10, whose digital device-free environment and syllabus covering everything from The Odyssey and Ulysses to Plato and James Baldwin — at a pace of one substantial book per week — recently drew the attention of the Wall Street Journal. Yet it’s always been true that you don’t have to major in anything to learn how to think, or in any case, to make a start of doing so.

Take the philosophy-and-literature YouTuber Jared Henderson, who in the video at the top of the post tells us how he began his self-directed study in high school. “I did what a lot of people would think is natural,” he says. “I went to a bookstore, and then I just found some books that I wanted to read.” The pieces of light reading he took home: Friedrich Nietzsche’s The Birth of Tragedy and Martin Heidegger’s Introduction to Metaphysics.

title: How China Might Target US Midterms
content:
No research shows Chinese propaganda or disinformation playing a pivotal role in the midterm elections, particularly when compared to Russia’s aggressive attempts. Yet significant blind spots exist. If it desired, Beijing is well-positioned to shape political debate through the WeChat app and through Chinese AI models.

Rather than shifting control of Congress, Beijing’s goal would likely be to reduce the presence of known Communist Party critics, particularly those serving in the Congressional-Executive Commission on China. Created by Congress in October 2000, the Commission monitors Chinese human rights and rule of law.

Several competitive races feature Commission members, including former Senator Sherrod Brown in Ohio and current Commission Chair Dan Sullivan in Alaska. House races in Iowa and Virginia involve current Commission members Zach Nunn and Jen Kiggans. Ashley Hinson, who is running for the Senate in Iowa, is on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, another Congressional body critical of the regime.

title: Independent Digital Media Is Not a Privilege Governments Can Revoke: The Fight to Save Egypt’s Mada Masr
content:
On November 11, Lina Attalah, founder and editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr, will face trial for the second time in just two weeks. This time, she faces charges of spreading false news, an accusation that has become one of the Egyptian government's most frequently used tools for prosecuting journalists. 

The trial follows a conviction on October 27, when Attalah was found guilty of managing an unlicensed news website. The Mada Masr team had repeatedly applied for a license, but their attempts went unacknowledged. The proceedings took place in a single hearing, which Mada Masr states included serious violations of her right to a fair trial. She was sentenced to the maximum fine of 3 million Egyptian pounds (approximately 55,000 USD), forcibly removed from the courtroom, and held for seven hours until the fine was paid. The court also ordered Mada Masr's closure and the confiscation of all equipment belonging to the organization.

title: Digitalpolitik, gibts das auch für die Gesellschaft?
content:
Digitalpolitik ist Gesellschaftspolitik. Wer unsere digitalen Räume und Werkzeuge gestaltet, gestaltet auch die Art, wie wir zusammenleben. Die OKF wie die breitere digitalpolitische Zivilgesellschaft bringt dieses Argument seit Jahren vor und setzt sich für Wege der demokratischen, gerechten und grundrechtskonformen Technikgestaltung ein. Mit KI, dem Bau von Rechenzentren und der Nachfrage nach Chips hat sich das Thema nun auch auf die physische Infrastruktur unserer Gesellschaft ausgeweitet.

In der Digitalpolitik dominieren heute aber andere Narrative. Auch das noch junge Bundesministerium für Digitales und Staatsmodernisierung verengt den Diskurs. Es darf bei Digitalpolitik aber nicht bloß um Souveränität, Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Sicherheit gehen. Geht es um digitalpolitische Programme, wollen wir uns nicht mit dem Eurostack und Deutschland-Stack zufrieden geben. Wir fordern den Gesellschafts-Stack.

title: Newsletter: Our 5-year anniversary, PHP2Shell, Sovereign Tech Resilience relaunch and more
content:
Email newsletter on 29 October: Our 5-year anniversary, PHP2Shell, Sovereign Tech Resilience relaunch and more

On 12 October, we celebrated our five-year anniversary with guests and friends from policy, open source, government, industry, civil society, and academia. It was a wonderful night to look back at our beginnings, and ahead to the future challenges for digital infrastructure and Europe’s digital sovereignty.

The critical vulnerability PHP2Shell sent shockwaves through the internet, reminding us all how important long-term investments into open source components are for our collective security. Good news though: The Sovereign Tech Resilience program has expanded to include four new services: memory safety transition, post-quantum readiness, supply chain security, and Cyber Resilience Act compliance. Applications are open.

If you’d like to find out about these updates as they happen, you can find the Sovereign Tech Agency on Mastodon, LinkedIn, and Bluesky.

title: EU Commission to probe supermarket cyberattacks
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission will assess how well supermarkets are prepared to handle cyberattacks after refrigerators in dozens of stores across at least six EU countries were taken offline.

EU Agriculture and Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen told POLITICO that the attacks would be discussed at the next meeting of its Security College to assess retailers’ contingency plans and their ability to respond to incidents.

“Europe’s food supply chain must be prepared for new and evolving threats,” Hansen said. “The repeated cyberattacks on supermarkets are deeply concerning, causing economic losses for retailers and empty shelves for consumers.”

The announcement follows dozens of supermarkets across Europe reporting disruptions to their refrigeration and freezing systems on Monday.

Incidents were reported in at least six EU countries — Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands and Estonia — with some retailers reporting that refrigerator temperatures had suddenly surged to as high as 50 degrees Celsius.

title: A year after the military coup: authoritarian practices dash Gen Z aspirations for a new Madagascar
content:
By Nciko wa Nciko

A year since Colonel Michael Randrianirina seized power in a military coup, Madagascar finds itself far from the refoundation that he promised. Instead, his first year in power has been marked by the military’s consolidation of power and the expansion of authoritarian practices. News outlets abound with commentaries assessing Randrianirina’s first year in power. The grievances and demands that led thousands of Gen Z protesters to the streets, including chronic water and electricity shortages and endemic corruption, remain unresolved.

Just like his predecessor Andry Rajoelina, Randrianirina has quickly turned to the law to unduly consolidate power, suppress dissent, instrumentalize anti-corruption efforts against political opponents, and shield his administration from efforts to bring accountability for killing and maiming protesters and for corruption. He has also weaponized the law to restrict civic space by characterizing freedom of association as criminal conspiracy and attempted to secure online mass surveillance powers over dissenting voices to make it difficult for them to critique his regime’s (mis)management of public affairs.

title: "Princes and Thieves" Author Matthew Cole on Jared Kushner & the "Secret Plot to Remake Middle East"
content:
Vanity Fair recently published an excerpt from longtime investigative reporter Matthew Cole’s new book, Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East.

The excerpt alleged that during President Trump’s first term, Saudi and Emirati leaders secretly put at least $2 billion into bank accounts and gave access to Kushner. At the time, Jared Kushner was serving as senior adviser to President Trump, his father-in-law. He is now Trump’s special envoy. Kushner’s lawyers responded by demanding that Vanity Fair retract the article and threatening legal action against the book publisher, Simon & Schuster.

Jared Kushner denied the report, saying, “The allegations made by this author are completely insane, categorically false, and never happened. We denied every one of these claims on the record, yet the author failed to provide a single shred of evidence to substantiate any of them.” His lawyers say no such bank accounts existed and that the allegations are unsupported by the verifiable evidence.

title: Three Detainees from January Protests Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, three citizens have been sentenced to death in Mashhad in connection with the January 2026 protests.

Based on information received by HRANA, the three individuals, one of whom has been identified as Matin Farnian, were sentenced to death in a joint case by Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, on charges of “moharebeh” (enmity against God).

The three were arrested by security forces in Mashhad on January 18 and 19, 2026, in connection with the nationwide protests. Following their arrests, they were transferred to Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, where they remain detained in different wards, including Ward 6/1.

Matin Farnian, 23, is a native and resident of Mashhad. HRANA is still working to verify the identities of the other two individuals sentenced to death in the same case.

HRANA’s investigation into further details of the case and the judicial proceedings remains ongoing.

title: Zambia: Widespread Repression in Post-Election Crackdown
content:
(Johannesburg) – The Zambian police and military forcibly disappeared, arbitrarily detained, beat, and threatened opposition members and supporters as well as lawyers, journalists, and government critics in the days before and after general elections in August 2026, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities have also yet to credibly explain or investigate the killing of an opposition leader in contested circumstances.

“Zambia’s government should break this dangerous cycle of repression,” said Ashwanee Budoo-Scholtz, deputy Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “The authorities should immediately halt the ongoing post-election crackdown, allow access to lawyers and provide medical care for those in detention, release everyone arbitrarily detained, and ensure accountability for abuses by security forces.”

title: Gaza’s Ceasefire Leaves Palestinians Trapped Behind a Moving Line
content:
UN rights officials warn that repeated displacement, attacks near encampments and restrictions on shelter materials are making return increasingly difficult.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 2 November 2026 (IDN) — A ceasefire may have reduced the scale of fighting in Gaza, but it has not ended the displacement of Palestinians. Nor has it given most families a realistic prospect of returning home.

The United Nations Human Rights Office, OHCHR, warned on 30 October that Israeli military operations continued to force Palestinians into ever-smaller areas of the Gaza Strip. Homes and public infrastructure were still being destroyed, displacement sites had come under attack, and families were being pushed away from areas close to the Israeli-controlled “Yellow Line”.

“The nightmare of displacement in Gaza is both acute and chronic,” said Ajith Sunghay, head of the UN Human Rights Office in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

Many Palestinians displaced before the ceasefire cannot return because their former neighbourhoods lie beyond the Yellow Line. Others have been uprooted repeatedly from places where they sought temporary shelter.

Venäjä on viime kuukausina kiihdyttänyt järjestelmällisiä iskujaan Ukrainan voimalaitoksiin kylmän talven alla. Se kohdistaa hyökkäyksiään myös kauas rintamalinjojen taakse vaarantaen siviilien hengen ja terveyden. Tavoitteena näyttää olevan yritys tehdä ukrainalaisten arjesta kestämätöntä.

title: The Killers of Journalists Are Getting Away with Murder. Governments Must Act to End Impunity.
content:
On the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists, IFEX exposes the gulf between governments’ commitments to media freedom and their failure to deliver justice. From the unprecedented number of journalists killed in Gaza to the question of who ordered the assassination of Daphne Caruana Galizia in Malta, those responsible continue to evade accountability. Meanwhile, civil society organisations and international institutions pursuing accountability face growing pressure.

The murder of a journalist is rarely an isolated crime. It is an attempt to suppress information, obstruct scrutiny and deny the public the truth. When perpetrators escape justice, sources are silenced, colleagues are intimidated and those who abuse power emboldened.

More than 100 IFEX member organisations document attacks, support journalists at risk and demand accountability. The scale of the crisis is stark: nine in ten cases involving the killings of journalists and media workers go unpunished.[1] In 2025, the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) recorded 129 journalists and media workers killed, the highest annual toll since the organisation’s records began in 1992.[2]

title: Suomi katsoo Keski-Aasiaan
content:
Viime vuosina Suomen kaupalliset, kulttuuriset ja poliittiset suhteet Keski-Aasiaan ovat tiivistyneet ja suomalaisyritysten vienti on moninkertaistunut erityisesti Uzbekistaniin ja Kazakstaniin. Keskiaasialaisten muuttoliike Suomeen on myös kasvanut nopeasti. Alue tarjoaa yksilöille ja yrityksille uusia seikkailuja ja mahdollisuuksia, mutta suhteiden kehitykseen liittyy monia kysymysmerkkejä.

Venäjän keisarikunta ja britti-imperiumi kilpailivat jo 1800-luvulla ns. ”Suuressa pelissä” Keski-Aasian hallinnasta. Brittiläinen maantieteilijä Sir Halford Mackinder määritteli vuonna 1904 esittämässään sydänmaateoriassa Keski-Aasian ja sitä ympäröivät Euraasian alueet maailman geopoliittiseksi ”kääntöpisteeksi”, jonka päätyminen yhden mannermaisen valtakunnan haltuun johtaisi pahimmassa tapauksessa länsimaisen vaikutuksen katoamiseen koko Euraasian mantereelta. Mackinder kannatti siksi ensimmäisen maailmansodan jälkeisessä Euroopassa Venäjän patoamista reunavaltioiden ketjulla. Entinen Venäjän keisarikunnan ja Neuvostoliiton eteläraja on säilynyt siitä asti tärkeänä geopoliittisena jakolinjana, jonka toisella puolella avautuu nyt varsin dynaaminen ja monikasvoinen maailma.

title: In the name of the father, the son, and AI
content: The hyperrealistic image on the wall of the Church of Saint Mary Magdalene in Novolukoml, Belarus, shows a young man in jeans, holding a laptop in one hand and a rosary in the other. It depicts Carlo Acutis, nicknamed the “cyber-apostle” and often described as the first millennial saint. Fittingly, AI helped create it. The image was created by three people: a photographer, a designer, and an AI engineer. It was blessed on 11 October by Archbishop Tadeusz Kondrusiewicz, the former head of the Catholic Church in Belarus. The parish described it as the first such image in the country. But who was Carlo Acutis? Born in London to Italian parents, the teenager became known for promoting Catholicism online, earning him the nickname “God's influencer”. He died of leukaemia in 2006, aged just 15. In 2025, Pope Leo XIV canonised him, making him a saint. Despite all the work involved behind the image, the use of AI as sparked criticism online. title: Voting in 2026 Is Getting an AI Slop 'I Voted' Sticker
content:
It’s a small pleasure, but receiving an “I Voted” sticker after casting my ballot is one of my favorite parts of the whole voting process. I slap the sticker on my chest and spend the rest of the day feeling like I accomplished a little something. I participated in democracy and everyone who sees me will know it. Artificial intelligence robbed me of that small joy this year and replaced it with a small horror. My “I Voted” sticker is AI-generated slop. 

Getting a little sticker when you vote has been a tradition in the US since the 1980s. It’s a symbol of the election cycle. People take selfies and post them or share them with friends. It’s a celebration of democracy and a small way to pressure people into going to the ballot box. 

The voting sticker has been subject to every kind of discourse imaginable. Are “I Voted” stickers worth the cost? Wondered Marketplace in 2020. A cemetery in New York has spent time and money tending to the grave of Susan B Anthony because voters coat it in stickers during voting season. In 2008, companies like Starbucks and Ben and Jerry’s ran afoul of election laws for offering free treats to people who showed their “I Voted” stickers.

title: Inside the Secretive, Contradictory World of Campaign Ads Funded by AI Super PACs
content:
Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published. Become a member and support our work here.

An online ad for Ben McAdams, the Democratic candidate for Congress in Utah, emphasised that he could be trusted because he “fought back against MAGA”.

In Texas, another ad promoted Republican candidate Chris Gober, calling him a “MAGA warrior”.

What’s interesting is that both ads were ultimately paid for with money from the same organisation – Leading the Future (LTF), a Super PAC which opposes regulations that “constrain” innovation in AI. The network has received US$125 million in funding in total from OpenAI president Greg Brockman, his wife Anna Brockman, tech-focused venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and a16z’s founders, Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings show. 

Directly opposing LTF is Public First Action (PFA), which calls for AI safety regulations and guardrails. PFA has received $40 million in funding from AI company Anthropic. 

Like the ads run by organisations funded by LTF, the Super PACs funded by PFA also ran ads that appeared supportive or critical of Trump depending on the voters they were targeting.

title: There is now an alternative to Russian gas – but not yet to soaring prices
content:
According to GIE AGSI, the public gas storage platform for European gas infrastructure, Slovakia is currently receiving 486 GWh of gas per day, while withdrawals are approaching 615 GWh daily. With the heating season under way, an increasing share of these withdrawals is going directly to household consumption.

The energy content of the gas currently in storage stands at 20.5 TWh, representing 54.28% of Slovakia’s maximum gas storage capacity. This is below both Hungary’s storage level (77.5%) and the EU average (75%). Only Latvia has a lower figure in the statistics, at 50%.

At the same time, Slovakia’s storage capacity relative to its consumption is considerably higher than the EU average. Of the 3.5 billion cubic metres that can be stored, the majority – approximately 2.75 billion cubic metres – is held in NAFTA’s storage facilities near Láb, close to the Austrian and Hungarian borders.

These facilities are ideally positioned to receive and store both Russian gas arriving via TurkStream through Serbia and Hungary – at least for the time being – and gas delivered from Austria, including LNG unloaded at terminals in northern Germany.

title: Indonesia Asks Russia to Stop Recruiting Its Citizens for Ukraine War
content:
Indonesia’s government has asked Russia to cease recruiting its citizens to fight in the war against Ukraine after new data showed a surge of Indonesians joining the conflict.

The growth in mercenary recruits comes amid Indonesian government concerns that citizens of the Southeast Asian country have been tricked into joining the Russian military under the guise of civilian employment.

"The Indonesian government has asked the Russian government to take the necessary steps to ensure that Indonesian citizens are not recruited into the military or other military-related formations in Russia through any means," Indonesian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Yvonne Mewengkang said in a statement reported Sunday by state news agency Antara.

Mewengkang said Indonesia requested to be added to a list of countries whose citizens are exempt from official Russian military recruitment, Antara reported, adding she expected the measure to be implemented “effectively and as soon as possible.”

title: After ProPublica Investigation, House Democrats Demand Answers on U.S. Citizens Detained by Immigration Agents
content:
What Happened: Citing ProPublica’s recent investigation, House Democrats are again asking the Trump administration to explain why hundreds of U.S. citizens have been held by immigration agents and how the government verifies citizenship during immigration operations.

In an October letter to Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, California Rep. Lou Correa and 39 other legislators demanded the administration share the number of citizens that immigration agents have detained and how the government is tracking such encounters. They also asked for more information about how agents are trained to verify citizenship and legal status.

title: When a bull falls for a donkey: what an unlikely relationship reveals about animal sexuality
content:
On an Ethiopian plateau, a bull called Achille formed an unusual relationship with a male donkey named Patroclo. They were observed spending time together, licking and rubbing against one another, and repeatedly having penetrative sex.

The animals’ names nod to Achilles and Patroclus, the Greek mythological figures whose bond has been debated for thousands of years: devoted friends – or lovers? A new study in the journal Current Biology asks something similar about Achille and Patroclo: why would two males of different species repeatedly choose each other as sexual partners when females of their own species are available?

Perhaps the more interesting question is why we find their relationship so surprising.

The researchers first noticed Achille and Patroclo while studying gelada monkeys in Ethiopia. Intrigued, they began observing the pair more closely.

They recorded 51 mounting attempts, 34 of which involved penetration. Patroclo took an active role, presenting his hindquarters to Achille and initiating contact. Unlike another male donkey that Achille approached, Patroclo did not show obvious signs of trying to avoid him.

title: Jouni Kemppainen: Myös köyhemmät ehdokkaat ansaitsevat päästä esille vaaleissa
content:
Varakkaat ehdokkaat saavat helposti ostettua itselleen näkyvyyttä somessa ja vaalimainonnassa. Yhtä tärkeää olisi päästää ne vähävaraisemmatkin politiikan tekijät esiin edes julkisilla paikoilla, kirjoittaa kolumnistimme Jouni Kemppainen.

Eduskuntavaalit lähestyvät, ja tuhannet ehdokkaat ja heidän tukijansa ovat aloittaneet uurastuksen, joka takaa tähän maahan demokratian, mielipidevapauden ja moniarvoisen keskustelun.

Mutta saavatko nämä kansalaisyhteiskunnan sankarit ansaitsemansa arvostuksen ja tasapuolisen tuen tärkeälle työlleen?

Eivät saa.

Omaa ja ystäviensä aikaa ja rahaa poliittiseen työhön käyttävät ihmiset saavat liian usein osakseen omitusta vähättelyä ja matalamielistä naljailua oman edun edistämisestä tai itsekkyydestä.

Aivan liian harvoin kansanedustajat, kunnanvaltuutetut tai vaikkapa seurakuntien hallintohenkilöt saavat kiitosta siitä, että hoitavat toistenkin asioita meidän puolestamme.

Demokraattinen päätöksenteko voi tuntua hitaalta junnaamiselta, mutta vaihtoehdot sille ovat edelleen vähissä.

Venäjän, Valko-Venäjän tai vaikkapa Yhdysvaltojen tilanne ovat siitä valitettavan konkreettisia esimerkkejä.

title: Koronapandemia paljasti heikkouksia pohjoismaisessa yhteistyössä
content:
Koronapandemian päätöksenteossa painotettiin kaikissa Pohjoismaissa aiempien yhteistyösopimusten sijasta EU-politiikkaan perustuvaa yhteistyötä.

Pohjoismainen yhteistyö kylmän sodan ajasta aina 2020-luvulle on keskittynyt hyvinvointivaltioidean pohjalle, ja maat ovat pyrkineet vahvistamaan ja vaalimaan yhteistyötään eri aloilla. COVID-19-pandemian puhjettua pohjoismainen yhteistyö jäi kuitenkin konkreettisemman Euroopan unionin yhteistyön jalkoihin.  

Kansainvälisen politiikan apulaisprofessori Laust Schouenborg esittää vuonna 2012 julkaistussa kirjassaan The Scandinavian International Society arvion, jonka mukaan koko pohjoismaisen yhteisön perustana on hyvinvointivaltioidea. Vaikka yhteiseurooppalainen integraatio on EU:n myötä levinnyt erityisesti työvoima- ja kulttuurialoille, hyvinvointivaltioideaan perustuva pohjoismainen yhteisö on pitänyt pintansa EU:n rinnalla.

Pohjoismaisen yhteisön erityispiirteisiin kuuluu esimerkiksi kansalaisten tasa-arvo, laaja liikkuvuus sekä edullinen terveydenhuolto. Näitä piirteitä on pyritty vahvistamaan vielä 2000-luvullakin erilaisilla yhteistyösopimuksilla.

title: Saimaannorppa valtaa takaisin vanhoja vesiään, kanta elpyy hitaasti
content:
Saimaannorpan kanta jatkaa varovaista kasvuaan, tiedottaa Metsähallitus. Leudot talvet ja kalanpyydyskuolemat hidastavat kannan elpymistä.

Uusimman kanta-arvion mukaan Saimaalla elää tällä hetkellä 545 yksilöä, ja kasvua viime vuodesta on 15 saimaannorpan verran.

Viime talvi oli poikkeuksellisen vähäluminen ja kevät tuli aikaisin. Tänä vuonna havaituista kuuteista lähes 90 prosenttia syntyikin apukinoksiin ja keinopesiin. Pesäpoikaskuolleisuus on sekin ollut viime vuosina suurta, joskin tarkka arviointi on asiantuntijoiden mukaan haastavaa.

“Talvien lauhtumisen myötä perinteiseen lumipesälaskentaan perustuvan kanta-arvion epävarmuus kasvaa. Siksi kanta-arviossa hyödynnetään nykyään aiempaa monipuolisemmin myös muita havaintoaineistoja. Jo aloitettua menetelmäkehitystä jatketaan uudessa LIFE-hankkeessa", kertoo Metsähallituksen Luontopalveluiden erityisasiantuntija Miina Auttila tiedotteessa.

Tulevaisuudessa tavoitteena on parantaa laskennan tarkkuutta matemaattisella mallilla, jossa voidaan hyödyntää laajasti erilaisia seuranta-aineistoja.

    At COP31, nations will try to find agreement on various issues, including climate finance for developing countries and a global “just transition” towards a cleaner economy.

Etäopetuksen päivä kokoaa perjantaina 6.11.2026 yhteen opettajia, opetuksen kehittäjiä ja muita verkko-opetuksesta kiinnostuneita. Kaikille avoimen verkkotapahtuman teemana on tänä vuonna Pedagogista muutosta luomassa etä- ja hybridiopetuksessa.

Päivän aikana kuullaan käytännön kokemuksia ja uusia näkökulmia eri koulutusasteilta. Ohjelmassa tarkastellaan muun muassa tekoälyn hyödyntämistä ammatillisessa opetuksessa, toimivan hybridiopetuksen ratkaisuja, virtuaalisia oppimisympäristöjä sekä verkkoyhteisöllisyyden rakentamista.

Mukana on myös kansainvälisiä näkökulmia. Stockholm Distans Online Schoolin Jenny Lilja ja Beata Lhotsky Enberg kertovat, miten etäopetuksella voidaan tukea paljon koulusta poissa olleiden oppilaiden opiskelua. Kvs-säätiön Kaisu John puolestaan esittelee medialukutaidon edistämistä Palestiinassa etäopetuksen keinoin.

Etäopetuksen päivä järjestetään perjantaina 6.11. klo 9.30–15.45 verkossa. Tapahtuman järjestävät yhteistyössä Kvs-säätiön Etäkoulu Kulkuri ja Suomen eOppimiskeskus ry.

title: Museums Don’t Need More Visitors. They Need More Contributors.
content:
Above: Anna Stolyarova with the mural Tolerance

On a wall in Amsterdam’s Nieuw-West district, a mural called Tolerance is fading away. Nobody is rushing to restore it. And yet it is still part of a museum collection.

That collection belongs to Street Art Museum Amsterdam (SAMA), a museum without a building. Its hallways are the neighbourhood’s streets. Its artworks are the walls. Its visitors are the people who live there, who are also its contributors and, as founder Anna Stolyarova likes to point out, its sharpest critics.

A museum whose collection is quite literally vanishing has had to face questions most institutions can put off. Who creates cultural value? Who decides what is worth passing on? And what is a museum for when the knowledge it needs already exists outside its walls? SAMA’s approach to citizen science in museums offers a challenge to the whole sector: let residents help shape what the museum knows, preserves and values.

title: New NORDIS report highlights lessons from Nordic media literacy initiatives
content:
A new NORDIS report reviews 14 media literacy events and campaigns across the Nordic countries, highlighting lessons learned and a growing focus on artificial intelligence. The partners now aim to build on these experiences by equipping teachers and librarians with tools to help young people navigate an increasingly AI-driven information landscape.

The new NORDIS report Literacy events and campaigns documents what the NORDIS partners Faktabaari, Faktisk.no (Tenk), TjekDet and Källkritikbyrån delivered between May 2024 and October 2026.

They are in short:

  • 3 events and 11 campaigns in Finnish, Norwegian, Danish, Swedish and English.
  • AI and recommendation algorithms as the common challenge to digital infomation literacy, from the Faktabaari AI Guide for Teachers (launched at the NORDIS Digital Information Literacy Forum in Helsinki, January 2025) to Tenk’s AI teaching package and search course in Norway and TjekDet’s “Hey Chat… Who Should I Vote For?”material ahead of the Danish election in March 2026.

title: HIKET in Brussels: Towards an EU-wide integrated approach to LULUCF monitoring
content:
Reliable and transparent information on carbon sinks and emissions is essential for effective climate policy. Yet significant uncertainties remain, and differences in national monitoring and modelling approaches make comparisons across Europe challenging.

The HIKET approach offers a potential way forward: integrating ground-based observations, satellite data, inventories and multiple modelling approaches into a common framework for independent verification, uncertainty assessment and policy-relevant scenario analysis. Building on existing European research infrastructures, this could provide a foundation for a more coherent and reliable EU-wide LULUCF monitoring system.

Many thanks to ForestNavigator EU project, The Directorate-General for Climate Action (DG CLIMA, European Commission), Open Geospatial Carbon Registry (OGCR) project & Project CAFAMORE for the invitations and the opportunity to exchange ideas and explore future collaboration!

title: Watch David Bowie Take MTV to Task for Failing to Play Music Videos by Black Artists (1983)
content:
The old vaudeville phrase “Will it play in Peoria?” has its roots in the late 19th century, specifically in Horatio Alger’s novel Five Hundred Dollars; Or Jacob Marlowe’s Secret. Like all of the books Alger wrote extolling the virtues of thrift, study, grooming, industry, etc., this one articulates a middle American bootstraps philosophy and rags-to-riches mythology, while giving the entertainment industry a colorful way to sum up the small-town audiences who embraced Alger’s strait-laced ethic, and who needed to be pandered to or they wouldn’t get all those big-city jokes and references.

Peoria has been many places in the U.S.—from Tulsa to Boise—but whatever the test market, the assumptions have always been the same: the American mainstream is insular, middle class or aspiring to it, culturally conservative, unfailingly white, and fearful of everyone who isn’t. Such demographic dogma has persisted for over a hundred years. Even when it is shown to be outmoded or plain wrong, broadcasters and journalists continue to play to Peoria, genuflecting to a static, populist version of the U.S. that ignores large, rapidly changing segments of the population.

title: Ukraine Needs Clear Rules and Safeguards for Private Intelligence Companies
content:
Ukraine is the Wild West for many private intelligence firms, and in some cases an overreliance on them has put Ukraine’s intelligence community in a vulnerable position. Yet, with effective oversight mechanisms, they could help accelerate Kyiv’s intelligence reforms.

Private intelligence firms collect and analyze information from open-source and proprietary sources to produce actionable intelligence for the strategic decision-making of clients, and their operations in Ukraine have introduced new technologies, intelligence, and analytical capabilities.

Colorado-based Vantor, for example, provides geospatial intelligence derived from high-resolution satellite imagery that can be used to map, monitor, and analyze military activity. Its information has been used to monitor the activity of Russian forces in Ukraine and document their war crimes. Another example is Palantir, headquartered in Florida, which uses an AI-driven data analytics platform to facilitate quick intelligence processing.

title: Mistral CEO: Europe faces ‘complete trap’ without frontier AI
content:
BERLIN — Europe risks falling into a “complete trap” if it focuses on industrial AI while leaving frontier models to the U.S. and China, Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch said in an interview Monday.

On the sidelines of the Digital Summit in Berlin, Mensch said Europe needs to build its own computing capacity and advanced AI models to ensure security. He added that Europe cannot assume it will always have access to the most powerful foreign models, pointing to the risk that the U.S. and China could deploy export controls on AI.

“The idea that we can build anything meaningful without owning the foundation of it, which are the reasoning models, the brains that can operate the factories, that can help design better systems … is, I think, a complete trap,” he said. “And we’re lucky that people realize this now, that this is not a viable way.”

In recent weeks, Mensch has emerged as a leading voice against European leaders’ shift away from building frontier AI models. In September, top EU leaders advocated building applications on foreign models to reap the benefits, instead of chasing frontier models.

content:

COP31 comes after a year in which the climate crisis has become even harder to ignore. In September 2026, the United Nations acknowledged for the first time that the world is set to overshoot its target of limiting global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels within the next few years. The warning came as global temperatures continued to soar with the last two months setting global heat records.

title: All Souls or just your cat's?
content: On All Saints' Day (1 November) and All Souls' Day (2 November), millions of Europeans visit cemeteries and light candles in memory of the dead. But few believe the dead can still reach them. While the dead are remembered in this Christian tradition that dates back to the 10th century, few people today believe the dead can still reach out to the living. But what about animals? A Pew Research survey across 10 countries found that people are often more likely to believe that living animals have spirits than to believe the spirits of their dead ancestors can help or harm them. The gap is the biggest in Türkiye, where 81% believe living animals have spirits while 21% think our ancestors can still reach us. In Spain, most people don't believe in either. So don't forget to light a candle for all our furry friends who are still among us!

title: “What Are They Not Telling Us?” Reminders to Prepare for Emergencies Fuel Anxiety About an Impending Crisis
content:
The posts claim that these announcements were made almost simultaneously and ask whether this means the whole world is preparing for war or another crisis. However, as Delfi’s investigation shows, some preparedness recommendations have been in place in many countries for years, while more recent information campaigns are linked to specific national civil protection and societal resilience plans, rather than an impending global catastrophe.

In October this year, posts began circulating on X, Threads and other social media platforms claiming that numerous countries around the world were, one after another, urging residents to prepare so-called 72-hour emergency bags or stocks of essential goods and supplies that would allow them to manage for at least three days without outside assistance. Reports that the US Department of Defense was planning to prepare military bases to operate for three months without external support added fuel to the fire.

These posts have reached very large audiences in a short time. For example, a post by an account called Whale News Daily on X has received more than 5.3 million views.

title: “Chaos” in the Air: Five Ways Voting Could Be Disrupted on Election Day
content:
As Americans head to the polls on Tuesday, voting experts are watching to see how the Trump administration’s unprecedented efforts to assert more federal control over elections will play out.

Since President Donald Trump retook the White House, his administration has tried to force states to turn over their unredacted voter rolls and to restrict mail-in voting. The Department of Homeland Security has used its resources to identify and prosecute noncitizen voters, an effort that has unfolded alongside the agency’s massive crackdown on immigrants.

The president has justified these steps by claiming, without evidence, that American elections are beset by fraud and that illegal voting is tipping the scales in favor of Democrats.

ProPublica’s reporters are on the lookout for what’s going right and what isn’t. We’re monitoring voter suppression and interference, election observers and poll watchers, extremism tied to the election, and ICE activity at the polls. Have you seen something?

title: Turulta Venäjä-ukaasi – näin kommentoi pormestari Piia Elo
content:
Turku luopuu vuodenvaihteessa 2027-28 pelattavien nuorten jääkiekon MM-kilpailujen isännyydestä, mikäli Venäjän maajoukkue osallistuu turnaukseen. Kaupunki kertoi päätöksestä sivuillaan maanantaina.

Urheilun kansainvälisen vetoomustuomioistuimen CAS:n perjantaisen päätöksen mukaan Kansainvälisen jääkiekkoliiton IIHF:n on mahdollistettava Venäjän osallistuminen MM-kisoihin.

Tulevana vuodenvaihteena alle 20-vuotiaiden miesten MM-kiekko järjestetään Kanadassa, ja seuraavat ikäluokan kisat on tarkoitus järjestää Tampereella ja Turussa 26. joulukuuta 2027-5. tammikuuta 2028. Turun kaupungin tiedotteen mukaan kaupunki vetäytyy isännyydestä, jos ei pystytä varmistumaan siitä, että Venäjä ei osallistu kisoihin.

- Toimimme arvojemme mukaisesti myös silloin, kun se tarkoittaa luopumista merkittävistä tapahtumista ja niiden tarjoamista mahdollisuuksista. Niin kauan kuin Venäjä käy hyökkäyssotaa Ukrainassa, emme voi hyväksyä Venäjän maajoukkueen pelaamista Turussa, sanoo Turun pormestari Piia Elo (sd.).

Kaupunki toivoo, että IIHF ja Suomen valtio löytävät ratkaisun, joka estää Venäjän osallistumisen.

title: Tuttu suku kärvistelee ja selviää Kinnusen uudessa romaanissa
content:
Eero Karisto

Uudessa romaanissaan Pitkä aukea Tommi Kinnunen jatkaa aiemmista romaaneista tutun suvun tarinaa. Vaikka kirjan maailmassa on paljon ilkeyttä ja vaikeutta, yleisvaikutelma on positiivinen. Kaikesta selvitään.

Suku tuli tutuksi jo Kinnusen esikoisessa Neljäntienristeys, ja se tavattiin myös romaanissa Lopotti.

Pitkän aukean taustalla vaikuttaa jatkuvasti jo esikoisessa kerrottu isän seksuaalinen suuntautuminen ja siihen liittynyt itsemurha. Homoseksuaalisuus on muutenkin näkyvästi läsnä Kinnusen tuotannossa.

Pitkän aukean kertojan, tuon itsensä tappaneen miehen pojan ajatukset kiertävät isän ympärillä, lapsuuden muistoissa, niissä iloisissa mutta myös todella surkeissa. Romaanissa isä tuntuu olevan enemmän läsnä kuin omat lapset. Kertojan ja isän suhde elää vain kertojan ajatuksissa. Omat lapset tuntuvat tietävän kovin vähän ennen heidän syntymäänsä kuolleesta isoisästä.

Osa romaanin tarinaa on ilkeän anopin ja ihan normaalin, jopa kärsivällisen miniän jännite. Kertojan sympatiat ovat täysin varauksetta puolison puolella. Äiti on yksiselitteisesti suvun pahis.

title: Whose Stories Get Remembered? WikiGap Nigeria 2026 Takes Another Step Towards Closing the Gender Gap
content:
Think of a woman whose work has changed her community, shaped an industry, influenced public life or opened doors for others. How much of her story can someone discover with a simple search online? How much of what she has accomplished has been documented, properly sourced and made accessible to the next person looking for her name?

For many women, the answer is not enough.

This is one of the reasons WikiGap matters. Across Wikipedia and other open knowledge platforms, the stories of women remain unevenly represented. Some are difficult to find; others have received little attention beyond their immediate communities. Their contributions may be known to the people whose lives they have touched, yet remain largely absent from the knowledge the rest of the world can access.

In Nigeria, WikiGap is an opportunity to do something about that absence. It brings people together to document women’s lives and achievements, encourage more women to participate in open knowledge, and create space for conversations about who gets represented in the digital world.

title: Guest lecture: Teaching difficult history in a polarized age, 19.11.2026
content:
How can we teach difficult history in a world increasingly divided by political conflicts, social media, and competing narratives? And how can Holocaust and genocide education help students develop the critical thinking skills needed to navigate a polarized society?

In an age of misinformation, echo chambers, and growing social divisions, teaching history is more important—and more challenging—than ever. While public debates often encourage simple answers and clear-cut distinctions between “us” and “them,” history education demands careful analysis, evidence-based reasoning, and a willingness to engage with different perspectives.

Drawing on twenty years of experience in Holocaust and genocide education in Denmark, Danish Holocaust educator Solvej Berlau explores the challenges and possibilities of teaching difficult history today. The lecture examines the development of Holocaust and genocide education in Denmark, including its introduction as a compulsory subject in 2023, and addresses a fundamental question: What does it mean not only to learn about the Holocaust and other genocides, but also to learn from them?

title: India Stall Opens in Central Asia’s Military Bazaar
content:
While attention mostly falls upon China’s inroads into Central Asia’s economic and security spheres, so undercutting Russia, India has emerged as a new seller of weapons as the region diversifies its military procurement.

In early October, Indian Defense Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh confirmed that India had exported its domestically developed Akash air-defense system to Tajikistan. The system can intercept aircraft, helicopters, and drones at ranges of up to approximately 25 km (16 miles). New Delhi also confirmed the export of the same system to Turkmenistan, which had previously been reliant on Russian- and Chinese-origin air-defense equipment.

Cooperation has also expanded in other security fields. In September-October, India and Kazakhstan held the Kazind-2026 joint military exercise involving approximately 60 military personnel from each country. This followed the India-Uzbekistan exercises, Dustlik-2026, held in April and a similar drill held with Kyrgyzstan.

title: Berlin unveils blueprint to catch up on AI
content:
BERLIN — Germany is unveiling its plan to catch up in the global AI race, but key details remain unclear.

Germany should become a “sovereign AI nation” by 2030 and narrow the gap with leading AI hubs in the U.S. and China, according to a report drafted by the government’s AI task force and obtained by POLITICO set to be released Monday.

“The next 12 to 18 months will therefore be decisive in setting the course,” read the report, which was due to be presented to the National Security Council and also at a summit on AI in Berlin.

Germany wants to secure access to the world’s leading models while strengthening European alternatives, particularly through expanded cooperation with France and Canada, according to the report. 

“We are leveraging collaborations with like-minded partners in the EU and worldwide (especially France and Canada) to benefit the German AI ecosystem and ensure sovereign access,” the report noted. “We will also use intra-European collaborations,” such as with French AI company Mistral, “to achieve this leverage,” its authors added.

At the same time, “AI made in Germany” should stand out through its focus on industrial AI with “highly specialized models,” the report read.

title: Ukraine: Russia’s increased attacks on energy and heating infrastructure ‘creating a deadly situation for civilians’
content:
• Civilian death toll increased significantly in recent months
  • Unlawful renewed attacks on infrastructure ahead of winter

    • Russia’s increased targeted attacks on energy and heating infrastructure risks creating a new humanitarian catastrophe for civilians ahead of winter, Amnesty International warned today.

    The civilian death toll during Russia’s full-scale illegal invasion has increased significantly in recent months, with October 2026 expected to be one of the deadliest periods for civilians in years.

    Based on prior Russian military attacks in the approach to previous winters, there is overwhelming evidence that the deliberate targeting of energy and heating infrastructure intended to cause civilian suffering will result in immense harm. The International Criminal Court (ICC) has indicted Russia’s Lieutenant General Sergei Ivanovich Kobylash and Admiral Viktor Nikolayevich Sokolov on charges of war crimes for allegedly directing attacks on Ukrainian electrical infrastructure.

title: January 2026 Protests: Supreme Court Upholds Death Sentence of Arman Marefati
content:
According to HRANA, the death sentence of Arman Marefati, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been upheld.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the Supreme Court upheld the death sentence of Arman Marefati, who is currently held in Ward 3, Hall 37 of Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. He had previously been sentenced to death by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, head of Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, on charges including participation in operational activities against national security, entering religious premises with the intent to cause destruction, and involvement in setting fire to a mosque and a religious seminary.

It is worth noting that the death sentences of two other prisoners, Mehrdad Mohammadinia and Ashkan Maleki, who were co-defendants in the same case as Arman Marefati, were carried out in June 2026. The two prisoners had been sentenced to death on charges of “collaboration with the Zionist regime and hostile governments,” “creating insecurity and public fear,” “destruction and arson of public property,” and “participation in operational activities against national security.”

title: Frontex is eyeing sweeping new powers
content: The EU's border agency Frontex should take charge of deporting migrants, the European Commission said last week. This would put an agency once accused of serious human rights violations at the heart of enforcing new rules to ‘return’ or expel people who haven't been granted the right to stay in the EU. The tougher EU talk on migration follows a harsher stance from right-wing parties who teamed up earlier this year to agree on the Returns Regulation to detain non-EU nationals who have been ordered to leave. They would then be sent to so-called “return hubs”, such as a centre in Albania for people expelled from Italy who can't be deported to an unsafe home country. Frontex currently cooperates with EU governments to remove people from the EU. It worked with them to deport some 64,000 people from the EU last year, chartering more than 220 flights, and reintegrating some 20,000 people back into their home country, which frequently involves paying them to leave Europe. The Commission foresees Frontex becoming far bigger and taking on more responsibilities. It wants to triple its staff to 30,000, including a new 17,000-strong ‘border and return reserve’ who could be deployed to reinforce

title: Tribal Leaders Warned Border Wall Construction Would Disturb Native American Remains. They Were Right.
content:
Lorraine Eiler stood in the blazing August sun, surrounded by reporters, to offer a warning. The Trump administration was racing to erect a second border wall across Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, southwest of Tucson. If the bulldozers came, she said, they were bound to disturb the final resting places of her family and Hia-Ced O’odham tribal ancestors.

“People used to live here,” the 89-year-old said.

Fifteen days later, her fears were realized.

ProPublica has confirmed that Native American remains were unearthed in Organ Pipe amid soil overturned by border wall contractors.

The discovery, unreported until now, was made on Sept. 8, the National Park Service said in a statement. “Following established protocols, the University of Arizona conducted an assessment and confirmed that the remains are human and align with tribal cremation practices,” the agency said.

The Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act governs the steps agencies must take following an inadvertent discovery of Native American remains on federal land. Those steps include halting any activity that contributed to the discovery until tribal communities are consulted.

title: TTT-Klubin marraskuussa ikäkomediaa, protestinaurua ja rytmimusiikin riemua
content:
Tampereen Työväen Teatterin ravintolanäyttämöllä TTT-Klubilla marraskuu on vuoden vilkkain kuukausi sekä esitysten että kävijöiden määrällä mitattuna. Kalenterissa on 19 tapahtumaa, joista kolme on jo loppuunvarattu, kuusi likimain täynnä, ja loputkin vetävät hyvin.

Ohjelmisto koostuu vierailuista komedian, stand upin ja musiikin tekijöiltä sekä emoteatterin oman tuotannon Nordic Noir – pimee komedia näytännöistä.

Viisikymppisten elämästä komedian aihetta löytää kaksikin esitystä. Johanna Tohnin stand up show Viidenkympin villitys aloitti kautensa jo lokakuussa täysille katsomoille, ja sama vire jatkuu marraskuussakin. Myös Kaisa Helan ja Heidi Kiviharjun käsikirjoittama ja esittämä Ikänäky – puolen vuosisadan bileet on saanut lipunostajat lupaavasti liikkeelle 13.11. ja 14.11. näytäntöihin.

Stand up -vierailuista nähdään kahdesti Iikka Kiven ankeille ajoille kapinallisesti naurava Protestinauru (5.11. ja 6.11.) sekä Roosa Maskosen, Saana Peltolan ja Anitta Ahosen Pyhä kolminaiseus, joka lupaa että ”kolmen naaraan Bermudan kolmio lataa lavalle estrogeeniöverit, girl powerit, naisen tuoksun ja koston sekä tyttöjen jutut” (12.11. tuplaesitys). Vastapainoksi voi halutessaan käydä katsomassa TTT-Klubin ikisuosikin Luolamiehen (7.11. ja 26.11.).


Keikkalavalla bluesia, jazzia ja rockia sekä maailman paras nordgrass-yhtye

Marraskuun musiikkivierailut aloittaa ennakkoon loppuunvaratulla keikalla SF Blues -yhtyeestäkin tuttu parivaljakko Dave Lindholm ja Pepe Ahlqvist (7.11.). Ensimmäistä kertaa TTT-Klubilla esiintyy tribuuttiyhtye The Miracle, joka asetteli kiertueensa teeman Queen-solisti Freddie Mercuryn syntymän 80-vuotisjuhlan mukaiseksi (13.11.). Amerikan länsirannikon isoa, sopivasti funkya ja aina viihdyttävää yacht rock -soundia hellii Timo Kahilaisen yhtye Just in Time, vieraanaan Heikki Hela.

Tamperelaisen jazzyleisön luottofonisti Masa Orpana esiintyy Honk-yhtyeellään New Orleansin tunnelmissa 27.11. Tampereella harvoin nähty Frigg-yhtye (14.11.) operoi puolestaan pelimannisvengin maastossa. Pohjoismaista kansanmusiikkia ja amerikkalaisia juurimusiikkeja yhdistelevä hienostunut ensemble konsertoi ulkomailla useammin kuin Suomessa. Maailmanmusiikkiyleisön keskuudessa Frigg on lajissaan kansainvälisesti arvostetuimpia nimiä.

title: Modern warfare spurs demand for new medical techniques
content:
Russia’s attacks on Ukraine’s health system and the changing nature of warfare have prompted innovative ways to protect wounded soldiers on the battlefield. 

From drone injuries and evacuations to fears of chemical, biological, nuclear or radiation attacks, there’s a major need for new technology and techniques to better support fighters — and citizens — caught in modern war zones.

Although banned under international law, attacks on health care facilities have become commonplace. The Kremlin has attacked health care facilities more than 3,000 times since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, according to World Health Organization data — and it continues to destroy critical health supplies.

In addition, double tap strikes — when a second attack is launched against people going to help those injured in the first — have also increased the risks health care personnel face on the battlefield. 

These new warfare tactics serve to psychologically break those fighting to protect Ukraine, former U.S. Navy SEAL Marcus Luttrell said. “To completely break down the society, you get rid of the energy and then the health care,” said Luttrell, a former Navy medic.
snippet: Russia’s attacks on Ukraine’s health system and the changing nature of warfare have prompted innovative ways to protect wounded soldiers on the battlefield.

title: Pretty privilege can save lives
content: There’s the yellow swallowtail, a large, bright yellow butterfly with a stunning tail. Then there are less eye-catching species, such as the Alpine grayling – a rather plain-looking, brown butterfly found in the Alps. Recently, more than 21,000 people from over 100 countries took part in a survey rating almost 500 European butterfly species. Their responses were used to create a “beauty index”. Bright colours, particularly yellow and blue, contrasting patterns, and large, serrated wings or tails scored highest. The species that scored highest also had more photos on Flickr and iNaturalist, and more Wikipedia views. They also had more genetic studies and published research. “We had expected this to be the case in terms of public perception,” said Elisabeth Kühn from the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ), who coordinated this survey for Germany, in a press release. “However, we were surprised to find the same pattern in scientific research.” It’s not just a butterfly thing. title: Former World Bank economist accuses Baltic States of irresponsibility but gets his facts wrong
content:
In one of them, the economist also links the Baltic States’ historical experience to the risk of the rest of the world facing a nuclear apocalypse. His original post garnered at least 621 000 views in just over a week.

“It is a strange world. Because three small Baltic countries have a population of 5.7 million (and a combined area smaller than that of some second-tier Chinese city), half of whom live in Europe, while another third are Russians who cannot obtain citizenship, and because they have trauma and bad memories of Soviet rule, the entire world of eight billion people is supposed to head towards a nuclear apocalypse and perish,” Branko Milanović wrote on X on the 19th of October.

After the post was published, people from the Baltic States pointed out factual inaccuracies, including questioning the population and ethnic composition figures he cited. Commenters also said that Milanović’s remarks echoed Kremlin propaganda narratives.

In response to the criticism, Milanović published another post on 22 October, clarifying that his original post had referred to ethnic Russians rather than non-citizens.

title: One Prisoner Executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz
content:
According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. HRANA has identified the prisoner, who was hanged at dawn on Sunday, November 1, as Iman Ashraf.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Mr. Ashraf had previously been arrested on a murder charge and subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.

title: Ukrainian could become Lithuania’s second official language – fake news circulated in the names of officials
content:
A fabricated news item circulating on Lithuanian social media appears to show President Gitanas Nausėda and Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys expressing views on the possibility of granting Ukrainian the status of a second official language. How was it established that the material was generated by artificial intelligence?

The fake report claims, citing alleged statements by Nausėda and Budrys, that they do not rule out the possibility of Ukrainian becoming Lithuania’s second official language and being made compulsory in schools.

According to Delfi.lt, the image circulating on social media attempts to imitate an article published by the news portal 15min, but was created using artificial intelligence. This is evidenced not only by the fact that the man pictured next to the president bears little resemblance to the foreign minister, but also by a digital watermark embedded in the image.

title: EU and Canada’s 6-month test of commitment
content:
MONTREAL, Canada — The European Union and Canada have agreed to build the closest possible relationship. Over the next six months, they will have to define what that means — and whether Canada can become the EU’s first, and perhaps only, associate member.

A summit in Montreal last week highlighted the urgency behind the budding relationship. Both sides say their partnership is positive and not directed against any country. But it is also driven by mutual need: to shore up supply chains, pool expertise and reduce reliance on the United States and China.

Mark Carney told POLITICO in an interview straight after the summit that the two sides should not be tailoring their partnership to cope with the potential reactions of other powers. “We’re not adjusting [based on] what the U.S. might think, what China might think, what … Russia might think,” he said. The goal, the Canadian prime minister explained, is to help both sides “withstand shocks” and prevent rivals from exploiting critical dependencies.

title: Monthly Report – October 2026: Human Rights Situation in Iran
content:
Executions and Death Sentences

During October, 71 male prisoners were executed by hanging in prisons across Iran. Of those executed, 30 had been convicted of murder, while 26 were executed on drug-related charges. One prisoner was executed on a rape charge, and the charges against eight others remain unknown.

Of particular concern, however, is the continued use of the death penalty for political or security-related offenses, a practice that has intensified following the recent wars. During the month, two individuals, including an Iraqi national, were executed on espionage charges. Four others were executed on political charges under the charge of moharebeh (enmity against God).

title: Australia: Solitary Confinement Harming Prisoners with Disabilities
content:
(Sydney) — Prison authorities in the Australian state of South Australia are harming people with disabilities by using solitary confinement, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today.

The 50-page report, “‘They Just Locked Me Away’: Solitary Confinement and Abuse of People with Disabilities in Prisons in the State of South Australia,” documents the use of solitary confinement on people with psychosocial disabilities, mental health conditions. It details broader problems facing people with disabilities in South Australian prisons, including inadequate access to individualized mental health care and lack of prison oversight.

content:

title: Beirutin taivas ei ole enää hiljainen

title: Nearly all Americans believe corruption is a problem. But will it decide the midterm elections?
content:
In a politically polarised American electorate, it can be hard to find bipartisan consensus on many issues. Ahead of the US midterm elections, however, there is one thing almost everyone can agree on: concern about government corruption.

A record 89% of Americans recently said in a Gallup poll that government corruption is widespread, with Republicans, Democrats and independents all in agreement (ranging between 83-91%). This marks a significant increase from 73% in Gallup’s polling from 2024.

Out of 132 countries Gallup polled on the question since 2023, only four have recorded higher overall levels of concern: Lebanon and Peru (both 92%), and Ghana and Nigeria (both 90%).

As much as cost of living issues have defined much of the recent campaign rhetoric, a recent Fox News Poll found that concern about corruption in government (88%) ranked higher among voters than inflation (85%) or gas prices (83%).

A CNBC survey similarly found government corruption to be the most important issue facing the country, above any concerns about the economy.

title: Markus Leikola: Onko Mamdanin tie Suomen tie – vai syökö eipäs-juupas-väittely tulevaisuutemme?
content:
Kun polarisoituminen yltyy, ei kannata vajota apatiaan tai huutopotkuraivareihin, vaan miettiä, miten tällaisessa maailmassa on aikaisemmin toimittu. Siis muutakin kuin verenvuodatusta ja koston kierrettä, mitkä toimivat vain lyhyellä aikavälillä.

Kansainvälisessä politiikassa on pitkään uskottu, että haukat tekevät rauhan, eivät kyyhkyt. Tällä tarkoitetaan, että kovan linjan poliitikot ovat juuri kovalla politiikallaan varmistaneet omiensa vankkumattoman kanna­tuksen.

Kun oma tukialue ei ole vaarassa notkahtaa, niin silloin on sisäpoliittista liikkumavaraa käydä strategisesti isoihin ja potentiaalisesti herkkiin neuvotteluihin vastapuolen kanssa. Pätee siis valtakunnanrajojen sisä- ja ulkopuolisiin vastapuoliin.

Omasta historiastamme muistutettakoon, että syksyllä 1944 Stalin kelpuutti Suomen johtoon ja rauhantekijäksi Mannerheimin, vakaumuksellisen antikommunistin ja monarkistin, jonka ainoat meriitit olivat sotapäällikkönä.

This question was at the heart of a presentation by Tri Astari, founder of Wikimedia Women Community (WikiPerempuan), at the Open Education Conference 2026 (OpenEd26), held virtually on October 27–29, 2026. Through a lightning talk titled “Bridging the Gap Between Learning and Contributing: Women in Open Knowledge,” the community’s experience in connecting learning, mentorship, and meaningful contributions to Wikimedia projects was shared with an international open education audience.

The presentation highlighted an important perspective on gender representation in open knowledge. Increasing the visibility of women is not only about creating more content about them, but also about ensuring that women have opportunities to become active contributors and creators of knowledge.

title: Human speech follows the same patterns as birdsong — new research
content:
In every culture, humans speak and sing to each other. We have created an astounding array of languages and musical structures across the globe. And yet, within this diversity, some fundamental sequence patterns are repeated. These are often referred to as “universal” patterns in human vocalization.

Our new research, published this week in Science, reveals that many of these acoustic patterns in human song and speech are also shared with birdsong.

The study compared the songs of 367 bird species with examples of song and speech from 52 human languages.

As researchers in animal behaviour and neuroscience and music, we (Logan and Jon) spent 10 years documenting the prevalence of universal human acoustic patterns in the songs of zebra finches.

When Kendra joined our lab during her PhD, she proposed we investigate whether these patterns are shared across other bird species as well.

title: Semen Padang Cultural Heritage Photo Walk: Documenting Industrial Heritage for Free Knowledge
content:
On July 24, 2026, a “Photo Walk” event was held within the cultural heritage site belonging to PT Semen Padang. Established in 1910 during the Dutch East Indies era, the company is recognized as the oldest cement plant in Indonesia and one of the oldest in Southeast Asia. Its grounds hold many stories regarding the history of the cement industry in Indonesia, featuring buildings and various relics that bear witness to the company’s evolution over the years.

Through this activity, participants are invited to take a closer look at various historical sites within the Semen Padang area. Beyond simply exploring and taking photographs, participants also have the opportunity to learn the stories behind the objects they encounter. In this way, every photograph produced becomes more than just an image; it serves as a means to document and introduce history to the wider public.

This Photo Walk activity is part of the Wikijalajah 2.0 project, supported by the Wikimedia Foundation. Through this project, participants are invited to explore historical sites and document them through photography, helping more people discover Indonesia’s rich history and cultural heritage.

title: Why you should treat charisma as a red flag
content:
Today’s crop of smooth talkers tap directly into a specific evolutionary vulnerability. Here’s how to defend yourself

Recently, I was alone in a bar waiting for a friend. To pass the time, I started chatting to a stranger. He had an easy, confident way of speaking, which I admired. We discussed topics I know little about: the instability of modern economies, the feasibility of commercial space travel, the likelihood of a coup in Russia. I found myself leaning in and asking questions: I felt as if I could learn a lot from this person. We eventually got to psychology, which is more my wheelhouse. I brooded about how easy it’s become for people to accept strange ideas. “Some people will believe anything,” he observed. “Some people even believe the Earth is round!”

I returned with more than new perspectives and connections. I had shared Wiki Club SATI’s journey on a national stage, spoken about my personal growth, and discovered how much a community can help us grow-not only as contributors, but also as people.

title: Forget AI, Europe has a plan to win the next tech revolution
content:
Draft strategy on quantum computing obtained by POLITICO shows Europe won’t repeat its AI regulatory playbook.

By PIETER HAECK
in Brussels

Illustration by Nicolás Ortega for POLITICO

A perennial also-ran in the global AI race, Europe now sees an opportunity to win what promises to be another technological revolution by learning from its mistakes.

Brussels is set to unveil the Quantum Act, a major piece of tech-sector legislation aimed at pushing EU countries to band together to attempt to stay ahead of the United States and China in quantum computing.

A draft of the November proposal obtained by POLITICO seeks to overcome factors that have constrained Europe’s ambitions in artificial intelligence, including a lack of funding to turn research into commercially viable and competitive products — and to scale globally.

Crucially, it also shifts focus away from regulating the technology to driving competitiveness — an acknowledgement of concerns that Europe overregulated AI and shouldn’t do the same in a field in which it is at the scientific forefront.

title: ‘Bunch of baloney’: calls grow for Cop summit reforms as countries on track to fail nature targets
content:
Cop17, focused on protecting nature and restoring ecosystems, concludes on Saturday with critics saying system allows ‘one idiot’ to stall progress

Calls are growing for major reforms to UN biodiversity summits as countries fail to deliver on their promises to halt the destruction of the natural world, with governments likely on track to continue their record of never having met a target in the 34-year history of the convention.

Two weeks of negotiations at biodiversity Cop17 in Yerevan, Armenia, concluded on Saturday morning with countries vowing to redouble their efforts to meet this decade’s targets, which include commitments to protect 30% of the planet for nature, restore nearly a third of Earth’s degraded ecosystems and reform $500bn (£410bn) of environmentally damaging subsidies.

Anslow, Richard J. et al. “Cometary impacts are an unlikely pathway towards the origins of life on Earth.” Scientific Reports. 

Carl Sagan eloquently said that we are all made of “star stuff,” but just how much of us is really comet vomit? title: AI search cites a narrower set of news outlets than readers visit
content:
When AI chatbots and Google's AI summaries answer people's questions, the sources they cite come from a narrower set of news outlets than the ones readers would have visited on their own.

Carnegie Mellon researchers Peter Carragher and Kathleen M. Carley found that pattern for ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Grok and Google's AI Overviews in most of the countries where they could measure it. As more people get their news through AI, that could hand more of the audience to fewer outlets and fewer owners.

To show the stakes, the researchers compared that gap with a merger. Paramount Skydance's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, which closed Oct. 6, put CBS News and CNN under one owner, and by their estimate it raised US media concentration by 9.9%. If every regular Google search ran through AI Overviews and readers went where its citations pointed, US concentration would rise 33.3%, about 3.4 times the merger's effect.

That's a thought experiment, and the researchers say so: It will take longer-term data to show whether readers follow AI citations. What they measured is the gap between what AI cites and what people read.
snippet: When AI chatbots and Google's AI summaries answer people's questions, the sources they cite come from a narrower set of news outlets than the ones readers would have visited on their own.

title: Dagbani Wikimedians User Group Celebrates Wikidata’s 14th Birthday in Tamale
content:
On Saturday, 24 October 2026, the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group celebrated Wikidata’s birthday in Tamale with a learning session, an editing activity, and a cake-cutting session.

The celebration brought together participants to learn more about Wikidata and how they can contribute to the free knowledge movement. The program focused on the basics of creating Wikidata items and adding statements, allowing participants to understand how information is organized and represented on the platform.

The training session was led by Alhaj Darajaati, who introduced participants to the process of creating Wikidata items. Participants learned about the importance of items and how they represent people, places, organizations, and other subjects in the world.

The session also covered how to add statements to Wikidata items. Statements help describe an item by providing information about its properties and values. This is an important part of contributing to Wikidata because it allows information to be structured and connected with other knowledge in the database.

Participants were also introduced to how to add references to Wikidata statements and the importance of references.
