title: EU tells capitals to halt their national social media bans for a year
content:
The European Commission is telling capitals across the bloc to pause any national laws that restrict social media access to minors, as Brussels seeks an EU-wide set of rules.

But Austria, the first country told to halt its legislation Thursday, lashed out at the order.

“It is unacceptable for Brussels to block member states from enacting national laws without presenting a completed European solution of its own,” Austrian State Secretary Alexander Pröll told POLITICO.

The Commission and national capitals have been seeking age restrictions for social media over the past year, citing risks to young people’s mental health. But even after the EU proposed a unified law, different countries have continued pursuing different approaches and age limits.

In September, the EU proposed the Kids Act, which would set the same standard across the union, placing different limits on access for those under the age of 13, and for those under 15. But multiple capitals continued to legislate their own bans, as countries like Greece and Denmark have said they don’t want to wait for the EU-wide law to be negotiated and implemented.

title: Activist in DR Congo Faces Military Trial
content:
More than three months have passed since plainclothes security officers arrested pro-democracy activist Clovis Kakule Mutsuva on July 18 in North Kivu province in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Mutsuva, 32, is awaiting trial before a military court on several charges.

The Allied Democratic Forces, a Ugandan-origin armed group active in eastern Congo, has been carrying out deadly attacks in the North Kivu city of Beni, near the Ugandan border. Mutsuva and other activists used videos and public speeches to call for a city-wide shutdown of public activities.

The shutdown, which was peaceful according to Beni’s mayor, occurred on May 14.Nonetheless, two months later Mutsuva was arrested and charged with incitement to disobey the law, criticizing public authority, organizing unauthorized demonstrations, insulting the army, spreading false rumors, and spreading false information on social media. The prosecution has accused Mutsuva of calling on demonstrators to “set fire” to the streets at night in protest of insecurity and to demand that the government protect civilians.

title: Digital Independence Day: Switch to alternative form services
content:
Organising an event and want to know whether potential participants are coming and if they have any dietary requirements? Or running an open call where makers can apply with their email address, phone number and a motivation letter as an attachment? Online form tools such as Google Forms are often used for this. But which tool do you choose if you don’t want to rely on a big tech company? And how do you make sure your audience’s data stays safe?

Many organisations use Microsoft Office 365 or Google Workspace in the office. Both platforms also include a tool for creating your own forms. And what makes these tools ridiculously handy on top of that is that the results flow into an online spreadsheet in real time, where you can immediately run your analyses. Still, there are major objections to using these two companies’ forms.

title: “Peak Greenwashing”: Two Bills in Congress Endorse Misleading Recycling Claims
content:
The plastics industry spent decades convincing consumers that throwing used products stamped with the “chasing arrows” symbol into a curbside bin meant they would be recycled.

Now, amid growing awareness that many of those items never get reprocessed, the industry is championing a pair of proposals in Congress that would give misleading recycling claims the support of federal law.

On the surface, the two bipartisan House bills promise transparency for consumers by establishing national standards for recycling and recycled content labels. 

But the legislation — promoted by oil, chemical and packaging companies that spend millions of dollars lobbying Congress each year — would forbid states from setting stricter requirements. That would neutralize efforts like California’s “truth in labeling” law, which bans the chasing arrow symbol on plastic products that contain toxic chemicals or that can’t realistically be recycled.

title: 70 years ago the Suez crisis exposed British relative decline. Today, the Iran conflict could be doing the same for the US
content:
Months after the US and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran, the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed. The UK chose not to get directly involved in the conflict. Nonetheless, it has been exposed to the crisis through record-high diesel prices as well as a spike in inflation.

This echoes an earlier crisis in the Middle East, as my recent research illustrates.

Seventy years ago, the Egyptian government nationalised the Suez canal, sparking the Suez crisis. The canal, which passes through Egypt from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean, was a vital link for ships travelling between Europe and Asia.

After its completion in 1869 by a French-led company, the Egyptian government held a 44% stake in it. However, financial difficulties forced Egypt to sell its shares to the British government in 1875, leaving Britain and France with substantial financial interests in the canal.

title: Suomi tukee UN Womenin aloitetta naisten osallistumisen vahvistamiseksi rauhanprosesseissa
content:
Suomi myöntää 200 000 euroa naisten osallisuutta rauhanvälityksessä ja rauhanprosesseissa edistävälle YK:n tasa-arvojärjestö UN Womenin aloitteelle. Suomi on ulkopolitiikassaan vahvasti sitoutunut ihmisoikeuksien ja tasa-arvon edistämiseen ja tukenut pitkäjänteisesti YK:n naiset, rauha ja turvallisuus -työtä.

Aloitteella vahvistetaan naisten mahdollisuuksia osallistua rauhanprosesseihin lisäämällä heidän työtään tukevien tiedon, työkalujen ja asiantuntijatuen saatavuutta. Lisäksi tuetaan jäsenmaiden ja YK-järjestelmän työtä Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuus -agendan toimeenpanemiseksi sekä edistetään aiheeseen liittyvää poliittista keskustelua ja vaikuttamistyötä. Työtä tehdään suoraan rauhanvälitystä tukevien valtioiden, alueellisten järjestöjen ja niiden rauhanvälitysryhmien kanssa.

”Yhteisenä tavoitteenamme on varmistaa, että naiset voivat osallistua rauhanprosesseihin täysimääräisesti, tasa-arvoisesti, turvallisesti ja merkityksellisesti. Tämä edistää kestävämpää rauhaa ja vahvistaa osapuolten sitoutumista neuvotteluihin”, sanoi valtiosihteeri Pasi Rajala New Yorkissa.

title: Niko Pyrhönen: Dealing with an influential ally
content: European public discussion about foreign political influence has developed around a familiar distinction. Adversaries, particularly Russia, are often covertly but demonstrably seeking to shape European politics from within. Allies, above all the United States, are partners with whom disagreements are managed through diplomacy – even if it is often conducted away from public scrutiny. Under the second Trump administration, this distinction has become increasingly difficult to maintain. Washington has not merely disagreed with European governments over defence spending, trade, Greenland, or Ukraine. It has increasingly taken sides in political conflicts within EU member states. Importantly, the dominant Trump administration narrative – defending freedom of speech and the will of the people against odious liberal elites – increasingly aligns with how the Kremlin justifies its political influence campaigns in Europe. Three recent cases from this year illustrate both the differences in how the two powers exert influence transnationally and the alignment of their near-term political goals in Europe.

title: US: New Hurdles to Having Votes Counted
content:
(Washington, DC) – US states’ use of a tool to verify citizenship that is marred by inaccurate and incomplete data is creating new hurdles for the right to vote with the midterm elections only days away, Human Rights Watch said today. The Supreme Court ruled in late September 2026 that states could use the tool, Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE), to screen lists of registered voters for citizenship status, at least for the time being.

“The use of the SAVE tool is causing new hurdles for some voters,” said Katherine La Puente, US democracy researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Sending vaguely worded letters as early voting began or offering federal-only ballots to some registered voters risks a discriminatory impact on people’s right to vote.”

title: Digital Independence Day: Switch to alternative video platforms
content:
Teachers, marketers and communications professionals often share videos with their network or audience. From promotional videos to conference recordings, educational videos and tutorials. For many, YouTube is the most obvious option. It’s easy, cheap and everyone knows it. But of course, using YouTube to host your videos comes with major problems. So this week: alternatives to YouTube during Digital Independence Day.

So what are the downsides of YouTube? First of all: YouTube collects data on your audience’s behaviour. If you send a link to the children in your class or the people in your network, you’re forcing them to hand over their data to YouTube. And that’s before we even get to the persistent algorithms, which are used, among other things, to suggest what to watch next once the video ends. Before you know it, they’ve fallen down some rabbit hole. It all makes sense once you look into YouTube’s business model: get people to spend as much time on YouTube as possible, and sell as many ads as possible. A model that, as we now know, encourages nasty, addictive and opaque practices.

title: Who mapped Africa? Debunking the myth that Europeans alone plotted the continent
content:
After the United Nations adopted a resolution in September 2026 endorsing a map that more fairly represents the size of Earth’s landmasses, author and journalist Moky Makura of Africa No Filter – a main sponsor of the Correct the Map initiative – asked: “What else about Africa is the world underestimating that’s also hidden in plain sight?”

It is a fair question.

The initiative brought attention to the way continents are distorted by projections that display our rotund planet on two-dimensional maps, something that has long made Africa especially appear far smaller than it actually is. But it left another assumption untouched: that European maps of Africa – which became the basis of how we see African countries today – are based solely on the observations of the Europeans who made them.

As an expert on the map history of Africa, I know that this is a misconception which deserves rethinking. Recent research by myself and others on colonial-era mapping of West Africa demonstrates that much of the geographical information these maps show is based on African observations. It’s just that Europeans largely took the credit.

title: Riccardo Alcaro: Transatlanticism from within
content:
Donald Trump’s transactional pursuit of US primacy and strongly nationalistic outlook have prompted a reappraisal of relations with Europe among US foreign policy thinkers, while the uncertain standing of US security commitments has prompted similar processes in Europe.

Such debates have in fact extended beyond the narrow remit of the foreign policy establishment into the political arena. Politics has thus acquired renewed centrality in transatlantic exchanges, so much so that the future of the US-European alliance will be severely affected by how ideological imperatives will be reconciled with the hard realities of geopolitics and economic security.

Ensimmäinen palvelukokonaisuus yhdistää kaksi toisiaan täydentävää kokonaisuutta: pääsyn tehokkaaseen suurteholaskentaan, tekoälyä ja kvanttilaskentaa yhdistävään hybridi-infrastruktuuriin sekä asiantuntijatuen, joka auttaa käyttäjiä sovellusten tarkastelussa, kehittämisessä ja ajamisessa.

Kvanttilaskenta voi mullistaa monimutkaisten laskennallisten ongelmien ratkaisemisen. Tämän mahdollisuuden muuttaminen käytännön sovelluksiksi ei kuitenkaan ole yksinkertaista. Monilta organisaatioilta puuttuu pääsy kvanttilaitteistoihin, erityisosaamiseen sekä niihin laskentaympäristöihin, joita tarvitaan kvanttilaskentaa hyödyntävien ratkaisujen kehittämiseen ja testaamiseen. Samalla monet lupaavat sovellukset edellyttävät kvanttilaskennan toimimista yhdessä suurteholaskennan ja tekoälyn kanssa sen sijaan, että kvanttilaskenta toimisi erillisenä teknologiana.

Tämän kuilun kaventamiseksi tarjoamme kaksi toisiaan täydentävää palvelua, jotka yhdistävät pääsyn suurteho-, tekoäly- ja kvanttilaskentaresursseihin sekä asiantuntijatuen.

title: AI agents to the rescue as students battle it out to win the Nordic AI Cup
content:
Aalto University doctoral researcher Yue Fang first won the Finnish national AI hackathon and then triumphed at the Nordic AI Cup final held in Reykjavik in October 2026. While using AI agents and reinforcement learning were a big part of the winning strategy, Yue thinks human judgement was crucial too. In our Q&A, Yue reflects on the hackathon experience, explains how his dog joined the action, and ponders a future as an AI entrepreneur.

The final was an intense 24-hour experience, and I had a frustrating start. Network problems cost me about two hours, so I was already behind before I could properly get going. With such a short competition, that felt like a significant loss.

Once things were running, it became a continuous cycle of ideas, experiments, and decisions. Later that night, I left my AI agent working, put my computer in the bathroom, and went to sleep. It continued running experiments and submitting validation tests overnight.

title: Für die digitale Zukunft Europas: Franziska Heine in das Advisory Board des Digital Commons EDIC berufen
content:
Gute Nachrichten für Freies Wissen: Unsere geschäftsführende Vorständin Franziska Heine ist in das Advisory Board des Digital Commons EDIC berufen worden. Das europäische Konsortium wurde 2025 gegründet und hat sich zum Ziel gesetzt, eine gemeinsame Infrastruktur für digitale Gemeingüter in Europa aufzubauen. Dazu gehören digitale Angebote, Wissen und technische Lösungen, die gemeinschaftlich entwickelt, frei zugänglich gemacht und von vielen Menschen genutzt und weiterentwickelt werden können.

Ich freue mich darauf, diese Entwicklung mitzugestalten und unsere Erfahrungen aus der Arbeit für Freies Wissen einzubringen. Denn eine offene digitale Zukunft entsteht nicht von allein: Sie braucht Zusammenarbeit, gemeinsame Verantwortung und Infrastrukturen, die Menschen in den Mittelpunkt stellen. Genau daran wollen wir gemeinsam mit unseren europäischen Partnern arbeiten.

Tämä Teams-tallenne on osa AI-kahvit-sarjaa, jonka on tuottanut Yleisten kirjastojen tekoälyosaamisen kehittämishanke. AI-kahveilla pohditaan tällä kertaa, mitä tekoälyn käyttö tarkoittaa tekijänoikeuksien näkökulmasta ja mitä kirjastojen arjessa olisi hyvä tietää.

Aiheesta puhuu juristi Gia Signell Kopiostosta. Hän käy läpi tekijänoikeuden perusteet ja sen, milloin toisen aineiston käyttöön tarvitaan lupa ja milloin ei, sekä tekoälyn käyttöön liittyviä kysymyksiä tekstien, kuvien ja muun sisällön tuottamisessa ja muokkaamisessa. Esimerkkeinä ovat muun muassa se, miksi täysin tekoälyn tuottama sisältö ei saa tekijänoikeussuojaa, miksi suojatun aineiston syöttäminen tekoälysovellukseen vaatii luvan ja mitä EU:n tekoälyasetus tarkoittaa sisällön käyttäjälle. Lisäksi huomioidaan tavaramerkit ja tietosuoja. Lopuksi esitellään kirjastoille tarkoitettu Kirjaston Kopiraittila -sivusto. Webinaari järjestettiin 28.10.2026.

title: Vammaisuus työkyvyttömyytenä varhaismodernin ajan Suomessa ja Ruotsissa
content:
Vammaisuus muodostuu suhteessa kulttuurisidonnaisiin odotuksiin terveestä ja ns. normaalista toiminnasta ja käyttäytymisestä. Miten ”vammaisuutta” hahmotettiin 1500–1700-lukujen yhteiskunnassa?

Esimerkiksi 1600- ja 1700-luvulla ilmestyneissä lääketieteellisissä teksteissä ja sairaudenhoitoon liittyvissä kansalle tarkoitetuissa oppaissa määritellään sairautta ja poikkeavuutta, ja sitä kautta myös vammaisuutta. Kuvaukset hyvästä, luonnollisesta terveydestä kertovat vastapeilinä siitä, mitä pidettiin ei-terveenä ja kehon tai mielen toimintaan liittyvänä poikkeavuutena. Niissä terveys merkitsi ennen kaikkea työntekoa haittaavan sairauden tai muun vamman sekä kivun puutetta.

title: ECHOES showcases CHPortal at SWOCH 2026
content:
SWODCH 2026 is the sixth edition of the International Workshop on Semantic Web and Ontology Design for Cultural Heritage which took place on the 26th October in Bari, Italy, as part of the 25th International Semantic Web Conference (ISWC 2026).

SWODCH is a series of annual conferences whose purpose is to gather original research on the design of conceptual models, ontologies, and Semantic Web (SW) technologies for Cultural Heritage (CH). The heterogeneous and multi-format data available in these domains call for principled methodologies and technologies to semantically characterise, integrate, and reason over data, as well as to support its retrieval, management, analysis, and visualisation. The workshop also welcomes studies addressing the philosophical and social analysis of CH data and knowledge representation models, as ontologies in this domain need to account for the historical and social dimensions of data. SWODCH aims to bring together stakeholders – scholars from Computer Science and the Humanities and GLAM professionals, representatives from CH institutions, etc. – who are involved in the development and deployment of concrete solutions for Cultural Heritage.

title: From Main Street to Capitol Hill, the Case for Democracy’s Library
content:
At a time when free speech is under attack and the public record is fragile, supporters gathered in San Francisco on October 21 to celebrate the Internet Archive’s work to preserve knowledge for all through Democracy’s Library, an initiative to make government information accessible to everyone.

Watch Recording | View Event Photos

Nancy Pelosi, Speaker Emerita of the U.S. House of Representatives, and Robert Reich, former U.S. Secretary of Labor, were among those offering congratulations and encouragement to the Archive at the celebration of “Democracy’s Library: Tools for Participation.”

“Preserving the data is essential to a democracy,” Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi declared from the stage at the Funston Avenue headquarters. “Lincoln said, ‘Public sentiment is everything. With it, you can accomplish almost anything. Without it, practically nothing.’ But for public sentiment to prevail, you have to know—and we have to show them where they can find out.”

title: Maakunnallisesti arvokkaat Paltvuoren laitumet suojeluun Taivassalossa
content:
Luonnonperintösäätiö on ostanut Taivassalossa sijaitsevan 17,7 hehtaarin suuruisen Paltvuoren laidunalueen. Maakunnallisesti arvokas perinneympäristö suojellaan luonnonsuojelualueena, mikä turvaa alueen monimuotoisen luonnon, arvokkaat laidunympäristöt ja pitkän kulttuurihistorian.

Paltvuoren laitumet muodostavat poikkeuksellisen monipuolisen kokonaisuuden, jossa vuorottelevat avoimet heinäniityt, metsälaidunalueet, hakamaat ja tammisaarekkeet. Myyjien vanhemmat Antero ja Maila Seikola ostivat tilan vuonna 1975. Kohde tunnetaan monipuolisesta lajistostaan sekä poikkeuksellisen pitkästä ja katkeamattomasta laidunhistoriastaan, jonka ansiosta se on kohonnut maakunnallisesti arvokkaaksi perinnebiotoopiksi.

”Paltvuoren laitumet osoittavat, miten tärkeää jatkuva hoito on luonnon monimuotoisuudelle tämän kaltaisilla alueilla. Vuosikymmeniä jatkunut laidunnus ja ympäristön hoito ovat luoneet alueelle arvokkaan elinympäristöjen mosaiikin, jonka säilyminen voidaan nyt turvata pysyvällä suojelulla”, sanoo Luonnonperintösäätiön suojelupäällikkö Vilma Kaukoranta.

title: A US-China-Russia Summit: What’s at Stake?
content:
Vladimir Putin’s proposal for a trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Donald J. Trump on the margins of the November 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit is alarming on two counts.

At first blush, it raises the specter of a new Yalta, and it threatens talks on ending Russia’s war against Ukraine without Ukraine and its European allies at the table.

Yet that may not prove the greatest consequence — such a meeting would most likely prove inconsequential, because a deal along those lines would almost certainly run counter to Xi’s and Trump’s more immediate interests (including their desire not to fixate on Ukraine or be upstaged by Putin).

Where it could prove consequential is in how the world interprets it.

title: Can Europe’s defence industry keep up with sovereignty, speed and scale?
content:
As the US-underwritten European security order is less certain, defence and security are in the spotlight across Europe. Capital is not the constraint: what the European defence industry lacks is production capacity, skilled people and faster contracting. Sovereignty is fast becoming a hard requirement embedded in law and contracts, and the Nordic countries, with Finland leading the way, are emerging as central players in this fast-moving, security-critical market.

Europe’s defence industry is currently fragmented. EU NATO-countries field over 170 different major military assets, compared with approximately 40 in the United States – for example, 14 main battle tank types in the EU versus one in the United States. Consolidation can help close that gap by unlocking economies of scale, reducing duplicative R&D spend and improving operational cooperation on the battlefield.

title: Victory! You Can Now Exclude Apps from Siri AI
content:
In the most recent update to Apple’s devices, iOS 27.2, the company has introduced a new setting to “Exclude Apps” from Siri AI, fulfilling one of our asks from our Encrypt It Already campaign earlier this year.

One of our main concerns with new AI features on devices is how those features interact with end-to-end encrypted content, particularly with secure messaging apps. Many AI features require cloud processing, and despite privacy protections engineered into these systems, the content of secure messaging apps may leave a user’s device without their knowledge. That changes the privacy concerns around using those tools. In a perfect world, users would be able to put a barrier up to ensure data from certain apps doesn’t leave the device. Here was our initial ask:

You should be able to tell the operating system’s AI to not access an app, even if that comes at the “cost” of missing out on some features. The setting should be straightforward and easy to understand in ways the Gemini and Apple Intelligence controls currently are not.

title: Video recording of COMMUNIA Salon: The Rodin Case
content:
Must the Musée Rodin in Paris release 3D scans of sculptures from its collection in response to a freedom of information request? This question lies at the heart of a years-long legal battle brought by American artist Cosmo Wenman with financial support from COMMUNIA. On 13 October, we hosted a COMMUNIA Salon to discuss the “Rodin Case” and its implications for access to cultural heritage. Below, you can watch the recording and read our analysis of the case, drawing on key insights from the discussion.

The dispute began in June 2017 with Cosmo Wenman unsuccessfully requesting access to the files containing Musée Rodin’s high-quality 3D scans of several sculptures by the eponymous artist—all in the Public Domain. The French Commission for Access to Administrative Documents (Commission d’accès aux documents administratifs – CADA) backed his request, but the museum continued to withhold the files. Wenman initiated legal proceedings and in April 2023 the Administrative Court of Paris (Tribunal administratif de Paris) ruled in his favour and ordered their release.

title: Silence Has a Cost: Answer the EU Copyright Consultation by 10 November | Knowledge Rights 21
content:
View this email in your browser

Three things, in short. Whether research can keep using AI tools without paying even more for publicly funded work. Whether a strengthened research exception works across borders, and beyond purely non-commercial use. And whether an EU Secondary Publication Right guarantees every publicly funded researcher the right to share their work openly, whatever the publisher’s terms.

The rules that govern access to knowledge should be written with the people who depend on them, not just for them.

Open Access Week is over for another year. The European Commission’s targeted consultation on copyright is not. The deadline has been extended to 10 November, so you still have time to make your voice heard.

Two areas at the heart of the knowledge community’s work are on the table: the use of copyright-protected content in AI and copyright in scientific research. Both will shape what researchers, libraries and institutions can and cannot do in the years ahead.

title: When the Fire Comes, Our Phones Have to Work. Condition 50 Puts That at Risk.
content:
In the hills of West Sonoma County, a fire can crest a ridge faster than an evacuation order can reach you. In our Hacienda Firewise Council, we practice phone trees, walk our escape routes and keep go-bags by the door. Every one of those plans assumes something none of us control: that when the power fails and the smoke rolls in, there will still be a signal.

Out here, that’s already a gamble. As leaders of ten Lower Russian River Firewise Communities wrote to Governor Newsom on October 21, our rural communications infrastructure is “already sketchy.”

By November 2, the governor must decide whether to accept California’s $1.42 billion federal broadband award with a provision called Condition 50 attached. If it comes down to signing or saying no, he should say no.

title: Israeli Elections to Global Movements: Tariq Ali, Rashid Khalidi on New Book "The Neck and the Sword"
content:
We get analysis of the Israeli elections, the upcoming U.S. midterms, the pro-Palestine movement and more from Palestinian American scholar Rashid Khalidi and Pakistani British writer Tariq Ali. They are co-authors of the new book The Neck and the Sword: Palestine’s Unfinished Struggle. The book, an extended conversation between Khalidi and Ali over two years, offers an overview of Palestinian intellectual and political history, drawing its title from a famous phrase used by the renowned Palestinian writer Ghassan Kanafani to describe the futility of “peace talks” between occupier and occupied, saying it was akin to a “conversation between the sword and the neck.”

Kanafani was assassinated by Israel in 1972, “murdered simply because his words were too dangerous for Israel to tolerate,” says Khalidi.

Public opinion about Israel has grown increasingly negative in the United States and across much of the world in the wake of the genocide in Gaza, and it’s “not going to shift back,” says Khalidi. “People have seen something that cannot be unseen. They’ve seen genocide. They’ve seen slaughter. And Israel has no defense.”

title: A Message from the Founding Families: Carrying the Torch Forward
content:
Eighty-five years ago, in 1941, totalitarian forces were aggressively advancing across the world. To address this challenge, First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt and Wendell Willkie, her husband’s Republican opponent in the previous election, came together to lead the formation of Freedom House, a philosophically and professionally diverse group of prominent citizens committed to the cause of liberty. At that pivotal moment in American history, when isolationism was prevalent, Roosevelt and Willkie set aside partisan differences in the shared belief that American leadership would be essential in the approaching global struggle for freedom.

And indeed, it was. After World War II, when Nazi Germany and its aligned powers were vanquished and Soviet communism emerged as a new totalitarian threat, Freedom House campaigned for the institutions and ideals that defined the modern democratic order, including the Marshall Plan, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and the NATO alliance. The organization also worked to advance the realization of the United States’ own democratic ideals, standing in steadfast opposition to McCarthyism and joining the fight for civil rights for all Americans.

Often portrayed as abstract, large, formal, distant, and quite technical, justice is a moral and ethical area, tied to institutions and legal statutes, and can seem a long way from mundane daily experience. But it is also a deeply practical underpinning for how most societies function. Without justice systems that work and are understood at the most fundamental level, economic mobility is threatened, socially marginalized groups have no recourse, and lack of trust hampers institutions and interpersonal interactions alike.

title: No Accountability One Year After Tanzania Election Violence
content:
One year after Tanzania’s contested 2025 elections, authorities have yet to make any arrests for human rights violations committed before and during the vote.

In the months leading up to the elections, the government intensified its repression of the political opposition, government critics, and the media. Authorities also failed to account for a spate of apparent enforced disappearances, including that of former Tanzanian ambassador to Cuba Humphrey Polepole, who was reported missing just weeks before the elections. Polepole had publicly criticized the ruling party, Chama Cha Mapinduzi, for not being “aligned with safeguarding human rights, peace, and respect for people.” His whereabouts remain unknown.

On and after election day, police and people in plainclothes killed hundreds of protesters and bystanders in response to widespread protests and while enforcing a five-day nationwide lockdown. A year on, the fate of many remains unknown as families have reported burying their relatives with no body.

title: The Weight of Gold: Capitalism and the Limits of Rebellion
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 28 October 2026 (IDN) — At first glance, Padraic McKinley’s The Weight (2026), starring Ethan Hawke and Russell Crowe, appears to be a familiar Depression-era adventure: a group of convicts, desperate for freedom, must transport a fortune in gold through the treacherous wilderness of Oregon. Dangerous river crossings, betrayals, uneasy alliances, and the ever-present possibility of death fill the journey. Yet beneath the conventions of the survival thriller lies something considerably more ambitious: a parable about capitalism, the exploitation of the vulnerable, and the terrible price exacted by a society in which wealth is valued more highly than human life.

title: Opintokeskukset ry: Oikaisu valtiovarainministeriön väitteeseen
content:
Valtiovarainministeriö julkaisi 26.10.2026 Julkisen talouden meno- ja rakennekartoituksen, joka läpivalaisee julkisia menoja ja niihin liittyvien sopeutusmahdollisuuksien mittaluokkaa. Kartoituksen tarkoitus on tukea julkista keskustelua ja poliittista päätöksentekoa.

Meno- ja rakennekartoitukseen kirjatut tiedot opintokeskusten vapaan sivistystyön koulutustoiminnasta ja rahoituksesta ovat virheellisiä ja harhaanjohtavia.

Opintokeskukset eivät ole kansalaisjärjestöjen, puolueiden ja ammattiliittojen ylläpitämiä oppilaitoksia, vaan sivistysliittojen ylläpitämiä oppilaitoksia, jotka saavat valtionosuutta.

Kartoituksessa väitetään, että opintokeskusten kanssajärjestäjien kustannusten huomioiminen voi johtaa jopa yli 100 prosentin valtionosuuksiin. Väite antaa opintokeskusten rahoituksesta virheellisen kuvan.

Todellisuudessa opintokeskusten valtionosuus kattaa alle puolet koulutuksen kustannuksista. Opetushallituksen keräämien kustannustietojen mukaan valtionosuus kattoi vuonna 2024 42 prosenttia opintokeskusten koulutuksen kustannuksista. Loput 58 prosenttia katettiin osallistujamaksuilla sekä ylläpitäjien ja kanssajärjestäjien muulla omalla rahoituksella.

title: Lawson United Cinemas will reopen United Cinemas Toyosu as “Lawson United Cinemas Toyosu” on December 4, 2026, featuring FLEXOUND Augmented Audio™ seat technology
content:
FLEXOUND Introduction

Lawson United Cinemas Toyosu will introduce FLEXOUND Augmented Audio™, an immersive premium seating system developed by Finnish company FLEXOUND™.

The system uses integrated speakers built into the seats to generate sound and vibration. Through vibration transmitted from the headrest and seat back, audiences can feel audio throughout their entire body, creating a highly immersive cinematic experience across all film genres.

The FLEXOUND system is already installed in cinemas around the world and has received positive customer feedback.

At Toyosu, FLEXOUND will be installed in 11 auditoriums with a total of 146 seats.

Lawson United Cinemas holds exclusive distribution rights for FLEXOUND cinema seats in Japan, and Toyosu becomes the third installation in the country following Odaiba and Yokohama Minatomirai.

Cinema Renewal

Along with the theater renewal, the theater will change its name from United Cinemas Toyosu to Lawson United Cinemas Toyosu.

The cinema lobby will also be renovated. Improvements include expanded merchandise sales areas, enhanced customer convenience facilities, and an updated layout designed to improve the overall guest experience.

title: Vieraantunut öljyprovissi Alberta äänesti asemastaan Kanadan liittovaltiossa
content:
Kanada on keskellä kauppasotaa Yhdysvaltain kanssa, mutta sen yhtenäisyyttä koetellaan myös sisältä. Maan rikkain provinssi Alberta järjesti kansanäänestyksen liittovaltiosta eroamisesta, mutta päätti lopulta jäädä. Separatismi silti tuskin katoaa. Mistä kauna kumpuaa? The Ulkopolitist seurasi äänestyksen syksyä 2026 paikan päällä.

Kanadan preerioilla illat pimenevät ja lehdet liekehtivät syksyn monituisissa väreissä. Rivitalojen siististi hoidetuilla pihoilla voi nähdä vuotuisten Halloweenin hirviöiden määrän lisääntyvän ilta illalta, vaan tänä vuonna ne eivät olekaan ainoita pihapiirien ja kadunvarsien koristeita. “Anna Albertan päättää” ja “Jääkäämme Kanadaan” -pahvikyltit sen kertovat, lokakuun 19. päivänä vuonna 2026 albertalaiset äänestävät siitä, eroaako provinssi Kanadasta.

“Preeria on ryöstetty,” luki Calgary Heraldin pääkirjoituksessa vuonna 1905, päivää ennen Albertan liittämistä Kanadan hallinnon alaiseksi. Niin kutsuttu läntinen vieraantuminen Ottawan keskusvallasta on yhtä vanhaa juurta kuin provinssi itse. Alberta, Kanadan valtionrakennusprojektin palanen. Preerialla asetelman ei tänäkään päivänä koeta muuttuneen, ei ainakaan tarpeeksi.

title: Raving, reading, and resisting in Ukraine
content: It could be Berlin or New York. One autumn evening, hundreds gather in the rounded hall of a brutalist building at Kyiv Polytechnic Institute. A DJ plays soft electronic music. Some drink coffee, others sit on the floor with a book. Nobody is dancing. They call it a book rave. Bring a book and read together. Sit with your friends and talk about books. Go to some of the classes and listen to a lecture about literature. Or simply listen to music and meditate. But in Ukraine, books have become more than a pastime. Over the summer, Russian strikes destroyed an estimated 13 million of them. In Kharkiv, a single drone attack burned eight million books at a publisher's warehouse, including school textbooks and children's stories. “Why attack books?” asks Svitlana, one of the book rave's organisers. To her, the destruction recalls the long history of Russian attempts to suppress Ukrainian culture, from imperial language restrictions to Soviet censorship and executions. title: Objection, your honor
content:
You've probably heard, at this point, about the big changes coming to Meta's AI scraping terms for business accounts. Nieman Lab had that scoop, and since then, small businesses, journalists, and artists using Meta products like Instagram have been raising the alarm. But if you're in the EU or UK, you might be in luck and can object to that use of your data, as some users have pointed out.

Earlier this month, Meta updated its commercial terms of use for business accounts to allow it to “use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta’s products. 

Many artists and small business owners that rely on Instagram and Facebook are livid at Meta granting itself permission to use their content, including from websites simply connected to their Meta accounts, to train AI. But for users in the United Kingdom and European Union, for now, there’s a way to object.

title: Lawyers for ‘King of the South’ Try to Chip Away at U.S. Drug Trafficking Case
content:
Attorneys for alleged South American drug trafficker Sebastián Marset have asked a federal judge to halt the search of a potentially pivotal cellular phone until the U.S. government explains how it took control of the device from Bolivia.

Marset, a Uruguayan national and self-proclaimed “King of the South,” was arrested in March in a pre-dawn raid in Santa Cruz, Bolivia. Soon after his arrest, he was expelled to Peru and then whisked to the U.S. where he faces money laundering, drug trafficking and narco terrorism charges.

Law enforcement officers in Bolivia seized three phones from the house where they arrested Marset. However, it has emerged that they seized a fourth phone from an adjacent house.

Defense lawyers say in their motion — dated October 23 — that “it is impossible” for them to “be certain as to the timing of the search and whether it was done at the behest of the DEA [Drug Enforcement Administration] or was otherwise valid under Bolivian law.”

They argue that they weren’t notified about the fourth phone, which was a potential key piece of evidence for months, hampering their efforts and raising questions about the integrity of the operation.

title: Meet ProPublica’s 2026 Class of Emerging Reporters
content:
ProPublica’s Emerging Reporters Program provides support and mentorships to college students who are pursuing careers in investigative journalism and need additional training and financial support to help advance their goals.

Participants receive a $9,000 stipend, a trip to the annual NICAR investigative journalism conference, occasional training and presentations by speakers. They’ll also be paired one-on-one with ProPublica journalists who can help counsel them on stories, build their connections in the industry and expose them to the varied paths that careers in investigative journalism can take. Past Emerging Reporters have gone on to work at The New York Times, The Associated Press, Fresnoland, Capital B, The Tributary and other outlets.

title: Tekijänoikeusbarometri 2026: Enemmistön mielestä luovan työn tekijälle kuuluu korvaus, jos teosta käytetään tekoälyn kouluttamiseen
content:
Taloustutkimuksen toteuttamaan Tekijänoikeusbarometri-tutkimukseen vastanneista suomalaisista 81 prosenttia on sitä mieltä, että tunnetun taiteilijan tai esittäjän persoonallista tyyliä ei saa hyödyntää tekoälyn tuottamissa sisällöissä ilman asianmukaista lupaa ja korvausta. Lähes kolme neljästä (74 %) on myös vähintään osittain sitä mieltä, että tekoälyn kouluttamiseen käytetyistä, ihmisten luomista teoksista tulee aina suorittaa tekijänoikeuskorvaus teoksen tekijöille ja esittäjille.

Tutkimuksessa kysyttiin ensimmäistä kertaa kirjallisten teosten syöttämisestä tekoälypalveluun. Vastaajista seitsemän prosenttia kertoi syöttäneensä kirjan tai sen osia tekoälypalveluun esimerkiksi tiivistettäväksi, käännettäväksi tai muokattavaksi. Nuorista vastaajista näin on tehnyt jo 18 prosenttia. Kirjallisen teoksen tai sen osan syöttäminen tekoälypalveluun ei ole sallittua ilman tekijän lupaa.

Kyselyyn vastanneista suurin osa on sitä mieltä, että luovan työn tekijöiden tulee saada tekemästään työstä korvausta sen mukaan, kuinka paljon heidän teoksiaan hyödynnetään.

title: Tekijänoikeusbarometri 2026: laittomien suoratoistopalveluiden käyttö lisääntynyt merkittävästi nuorten aikuisten keskuudessa
content:
Nuorten aikuisten keskuudessa laittomien suoratoistopalveluiden käyttö on lisääntynyt vuodessa merkittävästi, selviää Taloustutkimus Oy:n toteuttamasta Tekijänoikeusbarometristä. Barometrin mukaan Z-sukupolvesta eli vuosina 1997–2012 syntyneistä jo yli kolmannes (34 %) käyttää laittomia suoratoistopalveluja. Vuosittain toteutettavassa tutkimuksessa selvitetään muun muassa sisältöjen käyttöä sekä asenteita tekijänoikeutta ja piratismia kohtaan.

Laittomien suoratoistopalveluiden käyttö vaikuttaa olevan voimakkaassa kasvussa nuorten aikuisten eli 25–34-vuotiaiden keskuudessa. Niiden kautta sisältöjä on katsellut, kuunnellut tai pelannut jo 28 prosenttia vastaajista, kun vuotta aiemmin osuus oli 18 prosenttia. Myös nuorten eli 15–24-vuotiaiden keskuudessa tällaisten palveluiden käyttäjien määrä on lisääntynyt ollen nyt 31 prosenttia (vuonna 2025: 27 %). Kaikista vastaajista 13 prosenttia myöntää, että heidän kotitaloudessaan suoratoistetaan sisältöjä laittomista palveluista; viime vuonna luku oli kymmenen prosenttia.

title: Suuri kosminen hiljaisuus: Mitä Fermin paradoksi kertoo ihmiskunnan tulevaisuudesta? Osa 1
content: Tarkastelen Fermin paradoksia yhteiskuntatieteellisestä näkökulmasta ja esitän, että kosmisen hiljaisuuden ymmärtäminen edellyttää huomion kiinnittämistä sivilisaatioiden aikahorisontteihin. Vaikka galaksimme ikä ja planeettojen runsaus viittaisivat älyllisen elämän yleisyyteen, teknologisten sivilisaatioiden kyky organisoida pitkäjänteistä, riskejä hallitsevaa ja yhteistyövaraista toimintaa on yksi mahdollinen pullonkaula. Nykyinen kapitalistinen maailmantalous ja valtiojärjestelmä tuottavat lyhyitä aikajänteitä, jotka ovat ristiriidassa niin eksistentiaalisten riskien minimoinnin kuin vielä pidempää aikajännettä vaativan tähtienvälisen toiminnan kanssa. Keskustelen ajallisesta sosialismista ja maailmanvaltiollisuudesta tapoina institutionalisoida pidempi aikahorisontti, johon kuuluu myös sukupolvien välinen oikeudenmukaisuus. Lopuksi esitän, että ajallisen organisoitumisen vaikeus voi olla yksi Fermin paradoksin avaimista: harvinaiset teknologiset sivilisaatiot eivät välttämättä kykene rakentamaan sellaista aikahorisonttia, joka mahdollistaisi ensin oman säilymisen pitkällä aikavälillä ja sitten vielä jossain vaiheessa kosmisen mittakaavan toiminnan.

title: Serbia’s students defeat the machine
content:
The student list has won an outright majority in Serbia‘s snap parliamentary elections of 25 October 2026, ending fourteen years of rule by Aleksandar Vučić‘s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). The result is less a routine alternation in power than a verdict on a model of governance – and it leaves Serbia‘s divided Social Democrats with uncomfortable questions.

According to the preliminary results of the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK), the student list (‘Students Are Winning’) received 52.7 per cent of the vote and around 140 of the 250 seats in the National Assembly. The SNS-led coalition ‘Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia’ secured 39.2 per cent and around 104 seats. Apart from lists representing national minorities, which are exempt from the 3-per-cent-threshold, no other list entered parliament, producing the most concentrated assembly since the return of multiparty politics in 1990.

title: Suomi on kytkenyt itsensä irti todellisuudesta
content:
Suomi on sijoittunut kuusi vuotta peräkkäin maailman kärkeen YK:n kestävän kehityksen tavoitteiden vertailussa. Kansainvälisten kahvipöytäkeskustelujen Suomi on maa, jossa koulutus ja terveydenhuolto toimivat, yhteiskunta on vakaa ja laiton korruptio vähäistä.

Kärkisijoitus kuulostaa vaikuttavalta, mutta se kertoo yhtä paljon mittareista kuin itse kestävyydestä. 

YK:n kestävän kehityksen tavoitteet yhdistävät köyhyyden vähentämisen, terveyden, koulutuksen ja ympäristönsuojelun kaltaisia päämääriä. Käytännössä mittarit kuitenkin painottavat vahvasti sosiaalista ja taloudellista kehitystä, kun taas ekologiset reunaehdot jäävät taka-alalle.  

Kestävä kehitys on perinteisesti kuvattu kolmen pilarin mallina: ekologinen, sosiaalinen ja taloudellinen kestävyys. Tämäkin keskustelu sivuuttaa luonnon kantokyvyn, ikään kuin hyvinvointi voisi rakentua siitä riippumatta.  

Maailmalla ja Suomessa tätä ajattelua vahvistaa tarina talouskasvun ja ympäristöhaittojen irtikytkennästä. Päästöjen väheneminen esitetään todisteena siitä, että suunta on oikea ja että nykyinen talousmalli pystyy ratkaisemaan ympäristöongelmat teknologian, innovaatioiden ja markkinoiden avulla.

title: The impossible equation of being a researcher mother, striving to make ends meet
content:
How can we encourage women to pursue scientific careers? In recent years, a number of mentoring or awareness campaigns have been put in place to encourage French high school students to study maths, physics or engineering sciences, while they remain underrepresented in these fields. One of the last large-scale initiatives is the Filles et Maths program, launched in 2025, including work on gender bias, the implementation of “role models” or timetables featuring flexible hours.

The program was nonetheless met with criticism: while women remain under-represented in some disciplines, they also remain a minority in the highest positions across the board in the academic world, from mathematics to social sciences.

In France, gender inequalities are therefore not limited to access to scientific studies: they cut across all university careers and make many women leave French Higher Education and Research before securing tenure. This “drain” is explained by several factors among which motherhood holds an important place. A survey in Denmark illustrates that unlike men, one in three women abandon their scientific career after the birth of their first child.

title: In Brazil’s election, first-round voting was driven by resentment – in the runoff, it was guided by fear
content:
In the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, on Oct. 4, the politics of resentment prevailed. Frustration among those displaced from their jobs by automation and the newly self-employed – who sometimes wrongly see themselves as “entrepreneurs” – fueled the vote for the opposition of Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and favored far right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.

In the runoff on Oct. 25, however, the driving motivation shifted from resentment to fear of a return of the so-called “Bolsonarismo” to power. President Lula was reelected in a second round whose outcome could hardly have been anticipated from his lackluster first round campaign and Flávio Bolsonaro’s lead of 2.2 million votes. So what changed?

First, Lula took his campaign to the streets, where it had been largely absent in the first round. And it also moved into social media, where Lula’s presence had preiviously amounted to little more than a translation of analog campaigning into digital formats.

title: Watch: stronger eastern border regions through cooperation
content:
A new documentary follows Europe’s eastern border regions as they turn shared geopolitical challenges into practical ideas, stronger partnerships and more resilient communities through interregional cooperation.

The 12-minute documentary ‘Stronger eastern border regions: the Regio-Silience’ journey follows two years of collaboration among more than 30 local and regional authorities from Poland, the Baltic States, Finland and Norway. 

Supported by the Interreg Europe Policy Learning Platform, Regio-Silience brings regions together to exchange experience and explore practical responses in economic development, security, community resilience and regional cooperation. The film shows the journey from Antwerp to policy-learning activities in Olsztyn, Salla and Kirkenes. 

The documentary also shows how regional experience can inform the European debate on the future of the EU’s eastern border regions. It highlights the value of peer learning and cooperation in developing practical ideas, building lasting partnerships and strengthening resilience. 

Discover the full story: watch the documentary and read the article.

title: Ulkoministeri Valtonen tapaa Tanskan ulkoministeri Rasmussenin Helsingissä
content:
Ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen tapaa Tanskan ulkoministeri Lars Løkke Rasmussenin Helsingissä 28. lokakuuta. Ministerit keskustelevat muun muassa Ukrainan tukemisesta.

”Tanska on tärkeä pohjoismainen kumppanimme ja liittolaisemme, ja yhteistyömme on erittäin läheistä ja tiivistä. On aina hyödyllistä keskustella Tanskan kanssa ajankohtaisista aiheista ja Ukrainan vahvan tukemisen jatkamisesta”, sanoo ministeri Elina Valtonen.

Tapaamisen jälkeen ministerit osallistuvat ulkoministerien kuulemistilaisuuteen Pohjoismaiden neuvoston täysistunnossa, joka järjestetään Pohjoismaiden neuvoston 78. istuntoviikolla eduskunnassa. Kuulemistilaisuuden vieraileva puhuja on Ukrainan ulkoministeri Andrii Sybiha.

Tanska toimii kuluvana vuonna Pohjoismaiden ministerineuvoston sekä Pohjoismaiden ulko- ja turvallisuuspoliittisen N5-yhteistyön puheenjohtajana.

title: Joint Statement by President of the Republic of Finland Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister of Norway Jonas Gahr Støre on how to follow up the call for control over development of frontier AI models (englanniksi)
content:
Julkilausuman alkuperäinen kieli on englanti

Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a virtual meeting for world leaders on how to follow up the call for control over development of frontier AI models.

“AI is already transforming lives and bringing opportunities. But there was strong agreement in the meeting that governments cannot look away from the warnings about potential risks that come from across the AI ecosystem,“ said Prime Minister Støre.

“More countries have been joining the call for control. What we are aiming to do is sustain the momentum and try to identify realistic pathways forward. The time to act in managing risks related to AI and ensuring access to AI is now,” said President Stubb.

In the meeting, political leaders from 29 countries across the world shared their perspectives and inputs on international cooperation in AI risk management, how to ensure global trust, and their views on the path to establishing common standards.

title: Tutkijat: ilmastonmuutos on julistettava terveyshätätilaksi
content:
Ilmastonmuutos pitäisi julistaa terveyttä uhkaavaksi hätätilaksi maailmanlaajuisesti, ja tilanne on pahenemassa, varoitetaan tuoreessa Lancet-tiedelehden raportissa. Tuloksista raportoivat myös muun muassa Yle ja ABCNews.

Viimeksi kuluneet 11 vuotta ovat olleet mittaushistorian 11 lämpimintä. Yli 140 tutkijan laatiman Lancet-raportin mukaan helteisiin voitiin vuonna 2023 yhdistää arviolta 710 000 kuolemaa, joista yli 7o prosenttia oli ilmastonmuutoksen aiheuttamia. Tutkijoiden mukaan luku ylitti malariaan tai HIV:hin menehtyneiden määrän.

Samalla tarkastelujaksolla vuodesta 2016 vuoteen 2023 ilmastonmuutokseen voitiin raportin mukaan yhdistää lähes kolme miljoonaa kuolemaa.

Terveysriskit ovat vain pahentuneet vuoden 2015 jälkeen, jolloin toiveita herättänyt Pariisin ilmastosopimus allekirjoitettiin. Oikeudellisesti sitovan kansainvälisen sopimuksen tavoitteena oli pyrkiä rajoittamaan lämpeneminen 1,5 asteeseen verrattuna esiteolliseen aikaan.

title: Call for Session Proposals for the Rovaniemi Arctic Spirit Conference 2027 is now open
content:
28.10.2026

  • Share on FaceBook
  • Share on LinkedIn

    • We welcome proposals for sessions to be held during the Rovaniemi Arctic Spirit Conference which takes place in Rovaniemi, Finland on 24 – 26 May 2027.

    The conference is organized by the Arctic Centre at the University of Lapland and the City of Rovaniemi with several partners.  This year the conference is organized with a main theme “Our Arctic Home and Its Sustainable Future”.

    The Arctic region is home to humans but also many other species — both now and for generations to come. The conference will highlight different perspectives on how to ensure that the Arctic region remains a good place for everyone to live and call ‘home’.

    The first full conference day Tuesday 25 May is a policy day with keynotes and panels. The scientific and thematic sessions will be organized on on Wednesday 26 May. We welcome proposals for sessions that can be comprised of oral presentations or panel/round table discussions.  On Monday 24 May the program includes Arctic Innovation Forum and an opening reception.

    The length of the sessions will most likely be 90 minutes, including sufficient time for Q&A or other forms of audience involvement.

    • Rovaniemi Arctic Spirit -konferenssi järjestetään 24.–26. toukokuuta 2027, ja sessioehdotuksia otetaan nyt vastaan osaksi konferenssin ohjelmaa.

    Vuoden 2027 konferenssin pääteemana on ”Arktisen alueen kestävä tulevaisuus”, ja konferenssi tuo esiin erilaisia näkökulmia siihen, miten arktinen alue voi olla kaikille hyvä paikka elää nyt ja tulevaisuudessa. Konferenssin järjestävät Lapin yliopiston Arktinen keskus ja Rovaniemen kaupunki yhdessä yhteistyökumppaneiden kanssa.

    Ensimmäinen konferenssipäivä sisältää pääpuheenvuoroja ja paneelikeskusteluita. Toisena konferenssipäivänä järjestetään tieteellisiä ja temaattisia sessioita, joihin voi nyt esittää ehdotuksia. Jo ennen varsinaisia konferenssipäivä ohjelmassa on Arctic Innovation Forum maanantaina 24. toukokuuta, järjestäjänä Lapin kauppakamari.

    Sessioehdotukset voivat sisältää suullisia esityksiä, paneelikeskusteluja tai pyöreän pöydän keskusteluja, ja ehdotuksien tulisi sisältää joitain elementtejä konferenssin pääteemaan, arktisen alueen kestävään tulevaisuuteen, liittyen. Sessioiden kesto tulee olemaan noin 90 minuuttia sisältäen session lopussa aikaa yleisön kysymyksille ja keskustelulle.

title: UK budget 2026: Key climate and energy announcements
content:
• ‘New course on energy’
  • Energy bills
  • Warm homes plan
  • Fuel duty and EVs
  • CCS and hydrogen
  • Data centres
  • Other announcements

    • Chancellor John Healey has announced a “new course on energy” for the UK, focused on keeping bills low amid the global crisis triggered by war in the Middle East.

    As he laid out his first budget, Healey said the Labour government would still prioritise the expansion of clean power and remain “unshakably committed to net-zero”.

    The budget sets out what the chancellor calls a “radical reform of energy”, including a longer-term effort to “break the grip of gas on bills”.

    There are also a variety of short-term measures to curb energy bills, including a council-tax rebate and the removal of the gas “standing charge”, though these fell far short of pre-budget calls to tackle high prices.

    Moreover, in order to fund defence spending, the government is cutting £1bn from its “warm homes plan” and £700m from hydrogen and carbon capture and storage (CCS) projects.

    The budget also appears to cut up to another £4.7bn from the warm homes plan – as well as ending zero-rated VAT for solar panels and extending a “temporary” 5p cut in fuel duty.

title: Kestävyys syntyy yhdessä oppimisesta
content:
Minna Mattila-Aalto

Jos kestävä tuottavuus syntyy ihmisten kyvystä oppia ja uudistua, mikä on johtajan tärkein tehtävä?

Kaksi ensimmäistä kolumnia johtivat kahteen havaintoon. Tuottavuuskriisi ei ole ensisijaisesti teknologinen vaan ajattelun kriisi. Kestävä tuottavuus rakentuu aineettomasta pääomasta: osaamisesta, luottamuksesta, yhteistyöstä ja kyvystä uudistua.

Jos tämä pitää paikkansa, ratkaiseva kysymys kuuluu: mikä saa ihmiset oppimaan, uudistumaan ja muuttamaan tapaansa toimia?

Vastaus on johtaminen.

Valitettavasti johtamisesta puhutaan edelleen liian usein resurssien, rakenteiden ja päätöksenteon näkökulmasta. Ikään kuin johtajan tärkein tehtävä olisi varmistaa, että ihmiset tekevät asiat oikein. Tulevaisuudessa johtajan tärkein tehtävä on auttaa ihmisiä ajattelemaan uudella tavalla.

title: Beyond the Gallery Talk: How The Met Invites Artists to Think Out Loud
content:
What happens when you ask an artist not to explain a work of art, but to have a conversation with it?

At the Creative Museums Summit 2026, Isaac Poole, Associate Educator in Public Programs at The Metropolitan Museum of Art shared an exciting programme that set out to explore this question.

Most museum talks are built on interpretation: an expert stands before an object and tells us what it means. The Met’s Explorations series turns that around. Artists, playwrights, designers and choreographers are invited into direct dialogue with objects in the collection, responding through the methods of their own discipline. The focus is on their personal relationship with a work, not commentary about it.

The results have ranged from an audio guide that becomes a meditation, to a dance performed before a Tiffany window, to a comedy in which a marble muse talks back. Together they offer a model for reaching adult audiences that any museum can learn from.

title: Silence Has a Cost: Why Open Advocates Must Answer the Copyright Consultation
content:
Open Access Week may be over for 2026, but the need for advocacy and engagement for sustainable openness continues. If you have any energy left over after all the events, webinars and more, make sure you respond to the European Commission’s targeted consultation on copyright reform!

Much of the success of the Open Access (OA) and Open Science (OS) movements comes from the research sector’s own mobilisation. The readiness of researchers, institutions and funders to opt-out of publishing models based on the exploitation of copyright has had a transformative impact on scholarly communication.

At the same time, researchers use a wide range of content, so open access will only take us so far. Therefore, the value of getting the right conditions and support under national and European law cannot be overstated. Alongside providing funding for OA and OS infrastructures and mandating open publication of publicly supported research, wider laws like copyright are vital.

title: The Greens at 50
content:
Authored by Alberto Alemanno, this paper argues that European Green parties are facing not just an electoral setback but a deeper crisis of identity and purpose. While Greens have achieved significant political success over the past two decades, including helping shape the European Green Deal and entering government in several EU countries, they have struggled to adapt to a rapidly changing political environment.

The author highlights that Europe today faces interconnected challenges including geopolitical instability, energy dependence, technological domination by large corporations, democratic backsliding, climate impacts, and demographic decline. These issues create new opportunities for Green politics, but Greens have failed to explain how their values and policies address people’s everyday concerns.

At the heart of the problem is what the paper calls a “translation problem.” Greens have strong policy proposals but have been unable to turn them into a simple, compelling political story that connects with citizens. As a result, voters often perceive Green politics as technical, urban, and disconnected from issues such as security, affordability, health, jobs, and family life.

title: Commons Stories: Part 2
content:
The commons is a bonsai, and we are all its artists-gardeners. 

Sure, we could let it grow wild and unruly: it could be abandoned to the law of the jungle—left as a free-for-all—or fall victim to the tragedy of the commons, and shrivel due to overexploitation. 

But because we, as a collective, prune it from time to time, give it shape, direct and guide it according to common values and principles, placing intentional constraints, co-creating community-led boundaries (both explicit and implicit, written and unwritten) and shared governance structures, we will produce a healthy organism, one that can thrive for centuries. 

It is not a bonsai because of its diminutive size. On the contrary, the commons can be as ever expanding as the universe. It is a bonsai in the sense that it reflects the instinctive care humans often display towards our environment, our ingenuity, creativity and innovation in defining and supporting its underlying structure and deep network of contributors, and the respect for the shared, delicate ecosystem in which we all live, in harmony with the surrounding landscape.

title: Online Event: “Europa in der Datenfalle – Warum es mehr digitale Souveränität bei Webdaten braucht”
content:
Anyone searching the web almost always uses a non-European search engine. Anyone training AI systems needs web data – and here, too, large corporations from the U.S. and China dominate. Europe is currently heavily dependent on overseas servies within the digital sector. This is not only an economic problem but also poses a threat to European values and the democratic order.

That is why we keep asking some urgent questions:

  • Why is web data so important for the (digital) economy?
  • What opportunities does a European web data infrastructure offer – both economically and socially?
  • And what specific steps must Germany and Europe take now?

    • We provide answers in our paper commissioned by the Heinrich Böll Foundation, “Why We Need More Digital Sovereignty Over Web Data,” which will be published in German on boell.de on November 23.
    We will discuss these findings on November 24 in the following panel set-up:

  • Dr. Stefan Voigt, co-founder and board member of the Open Search Foundation e.V., co-author of the study
  • Maike Scholz, Group Compliance, Head of the “Digital Ethics” Squad, Deutsche Telekom AG

title: Social media is full of weird video game mashups. Where are they all coming from?
content:
AI tools are making it easier to modify and recreate games, raising questions about piracy, copyright and how far the technology could disrupt the industry

• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

If your social media algorithms have clocked that you’re into video games, something strange will have happened in the past few weeks. Your feed, like mine, will have been full of clips of streamers playing bizarre mashups of popular video games. Skyrim in Minecraft. Halo, except the main character is Mario. Skate 2 in Call of Duty maps. A flood of professional-looking fan-coded game mods that are mildly interesting to look at for 30 seconds, but ultimately inconsequential. Would I download a mod that lets me play Wii Bowling inside a zombie shooter? No, but I am very interested in where they came from.

title: Tutkimus: Tekoälylle juttelevat kokevat vähemmän stressiä kuin kirjoittamalla käyttävät
content:
Tekoälyn käyttö työpaikoilla ei muuta vain sitä, mitä työntekijät tekevät, vaan myös tapaa, jolla teknologiaa käytetään. Kirjoitettujen kehotteiden rinnalla tekoälyn kanssa keskustellaan yhä enemmän puhumalla.

Jabra Research Instituten WorkLife 2026: The New Shape of Work -raporttia varten haastateltiin yli 6 000 tietotyöläistä Saksassa, Yhdysvalloissa, Isossa-Britanniassa, Ranskassa, Puolassa ja Intiassa. Tutkimuksessa tarkasteltiin muun muassa sitä, miten erilaiset tekoälyn käyttötavat liittyvät työntekijöiden kokemuksiin työstä ja hyvinvoinnista.

Tekoälylle säännöllisesti puhuvat raportoivat 24 prosenttia harvemmin stressistä ja 23 prosenttia harvemmin uupumuksesta kuin tekoälyä vain kirjoittamalla käyttävät. Lisäksi he kertovat 37 prosenttia useammin kokevansa työnsä turvatuksi.

Tulokset kertovat ryhmien välisestä yhteydestä, eivät siitä, että tekoälylle puhuminen itsessään vähentäisi stressiä tai uupumusta.

Tekoälystä tulee keskustelukumppani

content:

Hier kommen fünf gute Gründe, für Wikipedia zu spenden.

„Es gibt doch jetzt KI – warum sollte ich noch für Wikipedia spenden?“ Diese Frage haben sich vielleicht schon einige gestellt. Die Antwort ist einfach: Wer möchte, dass die Antwort des eigenen Chatbots halbwegs stimmt, sollte für Wikipedia spenden. KI-Systeme und intelligente Suchmaschinen greifen Informationen im gesamten Netz ab – Wikipedia ist dabei eine der wichtigsten Grundlagen. Denn hier gibt es über 67 Millionen sorgfältig recherchierte Artikel mit nachvollziehbaren Quellen und eine engagierte Community, die das Wissen gemeinsam überprüft und ständig verbessert.

title: The Vibrant Color Wheels Designed by Goethe, Newton & Other Theorists of Color (1665–1810)
content:
Maybe it’s the cloistered headiness of Rene Descartes, or the rigorous austerity of Isaac Newton; maybe it’s all the leathern breeches, gray waistcoats, sallow faces, and powdered wigs… but we tend not to associate Enlightenment Europe with an explosion of color theory. Yet philosophers of the late 17th and 18th centuries were obsessed with light and sight. Descartes wrote a treatise on optics, as did Newton.

Newton first described in his 1672 paper the “revolutionary new theory of light and colour,” the University of Cambridge Whipple Library writes, “in which he claimed that experiments with prisms proved that white light was comprised of light of seven distinct colours.” Scientists debated Newton’s theory “well into the 19th century.”

One early opponent famously illustrated his rebuttal. Poet, writer, and scientist Johann Wolfgang von Goethe published Theory of Colors (see here), with its carefully hand-drawn and colored diagrams and wheels, in 1810. From Newton’s time onward, color theorists elaborated prevailing concepts with color wheels, the first attributed to Newton in 1704 (and drawn in black and white, above).

title: Court Should Curb Abuse of Grand Jury Subpoenas Targeting Social Media Users
content:
A federal appeals court should curb the government’s abuse of grand jury subpoenas to unmask social media users who criticize lawless immigration enforcement.

That is the message from the ACLU, EFF, and other civil liberties and trade groups who filed a friend-of-the-court brief in a sealed case in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia.

The case involves the government’s investigation of an anonymous Reddit user who commented on a post about an immigration officer in Minnesota. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) first issued an administrative subpoena to Reddit to unmask the user. When the user challenged the subpoena in court on free speech and statutory grounds (as many others have), DHS withdrew it. But then the government obtained a separate grand jury subpoena—a subpoena issued by a prosecutor to gather evidence to present to a grand jury before any criminal charges are filed—for much of the same information. The user then challenged the grand jury subpoena too, and the case is currently being appealed.

title: EU lawmakers slam new border force powers to surveil social media
content:
BRUSSELS — New powers proposed for the EU’s border police Frontex to monitor social media pose a threat to free speech, European lawmakers and civil society groups have told POLITICO.

The EU Commission’s proposal Tuesday for a major revamp of the coast and border patrol agency included a broad and explicit mandate to monitor social media for information that aids or encourages illegal border crossings into the European Union.

Social democratic Italian lawmaker Brando Benifei told POLITICO it was “legitimate” for authorities to remove online advertisements for human smuggling: “But a broad social media surveillance mandate goes much further, placing online speech under a border agency’s watch.”

After a 2019 monitoring tender with similar powers was revoked over criticism about privacy violations, Benifei said “the Commission now proposes copying ICE’s invasive online tracking,” referencing the much-criticized surveillance tactics of the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency.

title: EU: Frontex reform compounds risk of EU complicity in rights violations
content:
Responding to the European Commission’s proposed reform of the European Border and Coast Guard Regulation (the Frontex Regulation) that vastly expands the agency’s budget, powers, staff and mandate, without commensurately expanding its human rights safeguards and transparency obligations, Eve Geddie the Director of Amnesty International’s European Institutions Office said:

“The European Commission’s proposed changes to the Frontex mandate once again prioritize expanding the agency’s powers to deport, enforce border control, and operate beyond the EU without expanding the agency’s human rights obligations in turn.

“This includes giving Frontex new powers to carry out forced returns between non-EU countries, paving the way for a broader role in ‘return hubs’ in third countries. This reform compounds the risk of EU complicity in human rights violations and raises further hurdles to transparency and accountability. It should be rejected outright.

title: UAE: UN Secretary-General Candidate Whitewashed Abuses
content:
(Beirut) – Lana Zaki Nusseibeh, a long-serving UAE diplomat and foreign affairs official, has an extensive record of denying and whitewashing the country’s rights abuses in Sudan and Yemen, Human Rights Watch said today. On October 21, 2026, the UAE formally nominated Nusseibeh to be the new United Nations secretary-general.

“For years, Lana Nusseibeh has used her position to vehemently deny and divert attention from the UAE’s war crimes in Yemen and support for the abusive Rapid Support Forces in Sudan,” said Bruno Stagno Ugarte, chief advocacy officer at Human Rights Watch. “Her disinformation about the UAE’s rights record, particularly her dismissal of the UN’s own reports documenting the UAE’s links to the RSF, has seriously undermined justice and accountability for the victims.”

title: Loans don't grow on trees
content: Ever wondered what tobacco and banks have in common? Very soon, both will be warning consumers about the risks associated with their products. From 20 November, under new EU rules, adverts for consumer credit will have to include a clear and prominent warning: “Caution! Borrowing money costs money.” Very similar to the ones you see on cigarette packets. The requirement to warn consumers that loans don't grow on trees is part of new regulation to protect EU consumers taking out loans. Lenders will also face stricter requirements on the information they provide in credit adverts. This includes the total cost of borrowing and, where applicable, the loan's duration and repayment instalments. Misleading advertising will also be prohibited. The updated rules extend consumer credit protections to small loans of less than €200 and “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) schemes, which have become increasingly common in online shopping. There is one exception, though: shops that offer interest-free credit directly, without involving a third-party such as Klarna, as long as the purchase is repaid within 50 days. title: If You're In the UK or EU, Here's How to Object to Meta's AI Training
content:
Earlier this month, Meta updated its commercial terms of use for business accounts to allow it to “use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta’s products. 

Many artists and small business owners that rely on Instagram and Facebook are livid at Meta granting itself permission to use their content, including from websites simply connected to their Meta accounts, to train AI. But for users in the United Kingdom and European Union, for now, there’s a way to object.

Meta buried this change in its Commercial Terms, and Nieman Lab first reported on the change. The update was originally set to go into effect on October 30, but following backlash, Meta changed the effective date to November 20. Adding to the confusion, Meta then removed the word “train” from a list of allowed use cases, Nieman Lab reported, and limited those uses to “advertising and business products,” where previously it said that data would be used for all Meta products. Those terms still allow Meta plenty of leeway for scraping users’ data to develop its products, however.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro Flees Brazil After Election Defeat and Amid Fraud Probes
content:
Just three days after securing more than 59 million votes in a fiercely contested presidential runoff, Flávio Bolsonaro fled Brazil on Tuesday and landed in the United States, halting investigations at home over his alleged ties to a banker accused of financial fraud.

A senior U.S. State Department official confirmed Tuesday that the U.S. "State Department will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States."

Argentina's National Directorate of Migration (DNM) confirmed on the social network X that Flávio—son of the convicted former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro—crossed into Argentina through the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, which connects the Brazilian city of Foz do Iguaçu with Argentina’s city of Puerto Iguazú.

Accompanied by his wife and two daughters, Bolsonaro then boarded a private jet that made a short stop in Ecuador before landing in Miami, Florida.

title: How Cleta Mitchell Turned Trump’s “Big Lie” Into a Movement
content:
In July, not long before President Donald Trump delivered a primetime address questioning the legitimacy of American elections, the pioneering conservative election lawyer Cleta Mitchell and about two dozen of her associates logged onto a private video briefing with the White House.

Mitchell, who holds no formal position in the Trump administration, had been pivotal to Trump’s bid to challenge his loss in 2020, spearheading efforts to prove his claims of fraud and reverse his defeat in court.

After Joe Biden took office, when others abandoned the fight or scoffed as Trump clung to conspiracy theories, Mitchell doubled down, founding a grassroots organization devoted to rewriting election laws and rules to be more restrictive. Members of her group, the Election Integrity Network, were named to vital election-related positions in swing states and, later, in the second Trump administration.

The pre-speech briefing was an acknowledgment of just how consequential Mitchell and her organization had become. The White House had held similar sessions for key political players, such as governors, members of Congress and major press outlets.

title: No peace in Lebanon without strong allies
content:
It came as little surprise that Lebanon once again became a battleground in the regional war between Israel and Iran. Even without Hezbollah’s half-hearted rocket fire, Israel would have invaded the South again. No one knows the business of preventive war better than Tel Aviv. While Iran, under attack, has fared far better in the Gulf than initially expected, Israel has largely succeeded in imposing its agenda in Lebanon. Yet this is unlikely to bring Lebanon any peace. Instead, the country risks jumping out of the frying pan and into the fire: Iranian hegemony is simply being replaced by Israeli hegemony.

Lebanon’s reformist government, of course, frames things differently. Sovereignty is its watchword. The fact that Lebanon is negotiating directly with the Israeli state under US auspices is presented as an expression of that sovereignty. This, however, is an excessively optimistic assumption – one that misreads both Israel’s new security doctrine and the region’s emerging alignments. These separate negotiations will not bring stability. Instead, they will ensure that Lebanon remains divided, weak and occupied.

title: Eurovision 2027: Is Canada singing its way into the European Union?
content:
Officials are meeting this week for the 21st Canada-European Union Leaders’ summit.

It comes only a month after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen offered Canada associate membership. A draft statement from Montréal, where Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, von der Leyen and EU Council President António Costa met for two days to discuss strengthening ties, calls for an “ever closer association” that will result “in a more active foreign and security policy partnership.”

The talks follow a series of milestones in the relationship between the transatlantic partners, including the announcement in July that Canada was joining the Eurovision song contest. It’s the first country to do so since Australia entered in 2015.

Eurovision is held every year in May, with member countries submitting one original song. Over the years, the event’s format has changed from an exclusive jury vote to a viewer televote and today’s combination of both.

Sometimes, voting can become political, with viewers voting according to their geopolitical preferences or diaspora communities casting ballots for their former home countries regardless of the quality of the performance.

title: I’ve been talking to MAGA supporters for years, and here’s why some are sticking with Trump — and others are not
content:
President Donald Trump’s approval ratings are cratering. Even his Make America Great Again, or MAGA, diehards have reservations.

This fact was evident to me when I attended MAGA rallies in three states on Oct. 24-25, 2026. One was a Turning Point USA get-out-the-vote event outside Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.

Along with a few dozen America First stalwarts wearing white “America the Beautiful” caps, I sat on a wooden table under a small picnic pavilion listening to speakers such as MAGA activist Scott Presler and Trump-endorsed U.S. Rep. Dan Meuser. Meuser reeled off MAGA talking points, including the supposed threat posed by transgender athletes and bathroom use, immigrant voter fraud and the “billionaire anarchist George Soros.”

Remarkably, the speakers barely mentioned Trump. The audience clapped politely, but the energy was tepid compared to the many MAGA rallies I attended in 2024, when the Pennsylvania landscape was dotted with Trump and MAGA signs. This time I saw none.

The numbers bear out what I observed.

title: Revealed: UK relied on £2bn of ‘questionable accounting’ to hit its climate-aid goal
content:
• ‘Moving the goalposts’
  • ‘£1bn shortfall’
  • Accounting changes
  • Methodology

    • The UK has beaten its target to provide £11.6bn of climate aid to developing countries by 2026 – but only through “questionable accounting”. 

    As part of its obligations under the Paris Agreement, the UK pledged to give at least £11.6bn in overseas “climate finance” between 2021 and 2026.

    Now, Carbon Brief analysis reveals that around £2.1bn of the funds the UK counted towards this goal did not come from new spending.

    Instead, the government relabelled existing funding for development banks, private-sector investment and aid for Afghanistan, Sudan and other war-torn nations as “climate finance”.

    Without these changes, the UK would have fallen nearly £1bn short of its target.

    Carbon Brief’s analysis is based on numerous FOI requests and reveals the otherwise-unpublished details of the UK’s climate-finance spending.

    Experts and MPs say the use of “questionable” accounting shows the UK is “cutting corners” to hit its climate goals, while making unprecedented cuts to its foreign aid budget.
